commands.name: GetGeoLocation
commands.description: Gets the project location details: the project location, and the survey point's position, geo-referencing parameters, visibility and lock state (the lock from Archicad 26).

commands.name: GetSurveyPointTransformation
commands.description: Gets the 3x4 matrix that transforms points from the Project Origin coordinate system into the Survey Point coordinate system, row by row, and its inverse when it is invertible. Read only. Available from Archicad 27.

projectToSurvey.description: The 3x4 matrix that transforms a point given in the Project Origin coordinate system into the Survey Point coordinate system, row by row (12 numbers): x' = m[0]*x + m[1]*y + m[2]*z + m[3], y' = m[4]*x + m[5]*y + m[6]*z + m[7], z' = m[8]*x + m[9]*y + m[10]*z + m[11].

surveyToProject.description: The inverse of projectToSurvey in the same row by row layout: it transforms a point given in the Survey Point coordinate system into the Project Origin coordinate system. Missing when projectToSurvey is not invertible.

commands.name: SetGeoLocation
commands.description: Sets the project location details: the project location, and the survey point's position, geo-referencing parameters, visibility and lock state (the lock from Archicad 26). Omitted fields stay unchanged.

commands.name: GetProjectNotes
commands.description: Gets the Project Notes of the project (File > Info > Project Notes): client, project name, company, address, architect, draftsmen, project status, date of issue, keywords and notes.

dateOfIssue.description: Date of issue (free text, as typed in Project Notes).

commands.name: SetProjectNotes
commands.description: Changes the Project Notes of the project (File > Info > Project Notes). Only the given fields are changed; texts longer than the field Archicad stores are truncated.

dateOfIssue.description: Date of issue (free text, as typed in Project Notes).

commands.name: PrintView
commands.description: Prints from the current view.

grid.description: Print the grid. The default is false.

fixText.description: Use fixed text size. The default is false.

printArea.description: The area to print. The default is 'currentView'.

commands.name: RebuildView
commands.description: Rebuilds the current view.

regenerate.description: Regenerate the view. The default is false, meaning the view will not be regenerated, but rebuilt.

commands.name: GetSelectedElements
commands.description: Gets the list of the currently selected elements.

commands.name: GetElementsByType
commands.description: Returns the identifier of every element of the given type on the plan. It works for any type. Use the optional filter parameter for filtering. Objects that belong to another element (zone stamps, the parts of stairs and railings) are left out unless the IncludeSubElemObjects filter is given.

commands.name: GetAllElements
commands.description: Returns the identifier of all elements on the plan. Use the optional filter parameter for filtering. Objects that belong to another element (zone stamps, the parts of stairs and railings) are left out unless the IncludeSubElemObjects filter is given.

commands.name: GetElementTypeNames
commands.description: Gets the localized names of the given element types, as the running Archicad shows them (for example 'Wand' for Wall in German Archicad). The output is aligned with the input array of element types. Available from Archicad 27.

elementTypes.description: The element types to get the localized names of.

names.description: The localized name of each element type, aligned with the input, or an error.

name.description: The name of the element type in the language of the running Archicad (for example "Wand" for Wall in German Archicad).

commands.name: ChangeSelectionOfElements
commands.description: Adds/removes a number of elements to/from the current selection.

commands.name: FilterElements
commands.description: Keeps the elements that match all the given criteria: Archicad's flag filters (filters), layer (layerIndices), home story (floorIndices) and element type (elementTypes). Within one criterion any of the listed values matches; an omitted criterion does not filter.

filters.description: Optional. Archicad's own flag filters. An element is kept only when it fulfills all of them.

layerIndices.description: Optional. An element is kept only when it is on one of these layers (the layerIndex field of GetDetailsOfElements).

floorIndices.description: Optional. An element is kept only when its home story is one of these (the floorIndex field of GetDetailsOfElements).

elementTypes.description: Optional. An element is kept only when its type is one of these.

commands.name: GetDetailsOfElements
commands.description: Gets the details of the given elements (geometry parameters etc). Use the optional fields parameter to return only the fields you need and skip the computation of the others (for example floorPlanPolygons).

fields.description: Optional filter for the fields to return for each element. When omitted, every field is returned. Fields not listed are not computed at all, so listing only what you need skips in particular the floorPlanPolygons extraction, which regenerates each element's 2D drawing primitives and can dominate the execution time of batch reads.

detailsOfElements.description: One entry per input element, in the same order as the input elements array. An element that cannot be read gets an error entry in its place, so the position of an entry tells which input element it belongs to.

oneOf.description: Details of an element. When the optional fields filter is given in the input, only the requested fields are present; the required list below applies to unfiltered requests.

hotlinkId.description: The hotlink instance this element belongs to. Present only for elements that came in through a placed hotlink; such elements are read-only.

floorPlanPolygons.description: Cut-fill polygons as drawn on the floor plan (wall joins resolved by ArchiCAD). Only collected for construction element types whose floor plan symbol comes from a real cut through the element - walls, columns, beams and their segments, slabs, roofs, shells, meshes, morphs, curtain walls and their segments/panels/frames, stairs and their risers/treads/structures. Absent for every other type, when the element has no cut fill, or when the floor plan database is not accessible.

commands.name: SetDetailsOfElements
commands.description: Sets the details of the given elements (floor, layer, order, Element ID etc).

id.description: The Element ID (the ID field of the element's Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels). The same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id.

commands.name: GetElementCategories
commands.description: Lists the element categories of the project (Structural Function, Position, Renovation Status, Renovation Filter and, in the German version, BRI) with their possible values. The names of the categories and values are localized: identify a category by its type and a value by its categoryValueId, never by name.

categories.description: The element categories of the project, each with its possible values.

name.description: The localized name of the category, for display only.

values.description: The possible values of the category.

name.description: The localized name of the value, for display only.

isVisibleOnUI.description: The value is offered in the settings dialogs of Archicad.

usableAsCriteria.description: The value can be used as a criterion, for example in Find & Select and in Graphic Override rules.

commands.name: GetCategoryValuesOfElements
commands.description: Gets the category values (Structural Function, Position, Renovation Status ...) of the given elements, optionally only for the given category types. An element that has none of the requested categories (an annotation, for example) gets an error item. The names are localized: use the type and the categoryValueId in scripts.

categories.description: The categories to read. Left out: every category the element has.

categoryValuesOfElements.description: The category values of each element, in the order of the input. A category the element does not have is left out of its list; an element that does not exist or has none of the requested categories (an annotation, for example) is represented by an error object.

name.description: The localized name of the value, for display only.

commands.name: SetCategoryValuesOfElements
commands.description: Sets the category values (Structural Function, Position, Renovation Status ...) of the given elements, one element and one category per item, in a single undoable step. The value must belong to the given category, as GetElementCategories lists them; an element without that category gets a failed execution result. The names are localized: use the type and the categoryValueId in scripts.

elementCategoryValues.description: The category values to set: one element and one category per item. The same element can appear in several items, one per category.

categoryValueId.description: A value of the category given by type, as GetElementCategories lists them.

executionResults.description: One result per item of the input, in the same order.

commands.name: Get3DBoundingBoxes
commands.description: Get the 3D bounding box of elements. The bounding box is calculated from the global origin in the 3D view. The output is the array of the bounding boxes respective to the input array of elements.

commands.name: ConvertRevealOffsets
commands.description: Converts the reveal depth offset of windows and doors placed in walls between the two references Archicad uses: measured from the core skin of a composite wall, or from the wall side. Give exactly one of coreOffset or sideOffset per opening; both values are returned. For walls with a basic structure the two values are equal. The output is aligned with the input array of openings. Available from Archicad 27.

openings.description: Windows and doors placed in walls, each with exactly one of coreOffset or sideOffset.

elementId.description: A window or door placed in a wall.

coreOffset.description: Reveal depth offset measured from the core skin of the owner wall, to convert to the wall side reference.

sideOffset.description: Reveal depth offset measured from the side of the owner wall, to convert to the core skin reference.

revealOffsets.description: The reveal depth offset of each opening in both references, aligned with the input, or an error.

coreOffset.description: Reveal depth offset measured from the core skin of the owner wall.

sideOffset.description: Reveal depth offset measured from the side of the owner wall.

commands.name: Get3DGeometryOfElements
commands.description: Gets the 3D geometry of elements as the solid bodies of their 3D model: a vertex list in world coordinates and the planar faces (with their holes) referencing it, each face with its surface attribute when that is a project attribute. The bodies of the subelements of a Stair, Railing or Curtain Wall, and of the segments of a Column or Beam, are included. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. The 3D model of the elements is generated as needed, so many elements can take a while.

geometries3D.description: The 3D geometry of each element, aligned with the input: the solid bodies of its 3D model, or an error.

bodies.description: The solid bodies of the element's 3D model, including those of its subelements for a Stair, Railing or Curtain Wall, and of its segments for a Column or Beam. Empty when the element has no solid 3D model (for example a 2D element, or one filtered out of the 3D view).

commands.name: GetElementAtCoordinate
commands.description: Finds the element of the given polygonal type (for example Slab, Roof, Mesh, Zone or Hatch) at a coordinate of the floor plan of the current database, the way a click there would. Use the optional filters parameter (the values of FilterElements) to consider only, for example, the elements visible by layer, and the optional z parameter to give the elevation of the point. Returns found: false when there is no such element. Useful together with GetPointFromUser.

elementType.description: The type of the element to look for. Only polygonal element types can be searched, for example Slab, Roof, Mesh, Zone or Hatch.

coordinate.description: The point to search at, in the project's coordinates, on the floor plan of the current database.

z.description: Optional. The elevation of the search point, handed to Archicad together with the coordinate. Default is 0.

filters.description: Optional. Only an element passing every given filter is found (the same values as FilterElements accepts).

found.description: True when an element of the given type was found at the coordinate.

elementId.description: The identifier of the found element. Absent when nothing was found.

commands.name: GetQuantitiesOfElements
commands.description: Gets the quantities of the given elements calculated by Archicad (volumes, surfaces, lengths etc.), together with the volume and projected area per building material (one item per skin of composite and complex profile elements, one item for basic elements). Supported types: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Zone, ColumnSegment, BeamSegment. Use the optional minOpeningSize parameter to control the conditional values, and calculateInOneCall to calculate all the elements in one Archicad call.

minOpeningSize.description: Optional minimum opening size in square meters. Openings smaller than this are not subtracted when the conditional values (for example volumeConditional of a Wall) are calculated. Archicad only uses it for walls. Default value is 0, so every opening is subtracted.

calculateInOneCall.description: Optional. When true, Archicad calculates the quantities of all the supported elements in one call instead of one call per element, which can be faster for many elements. The output has the same format. If that one call fails, every supported element gets the same error. Default value is false.

quantitiesOfElements.description: The quantities of the elements, in the order of the given elements. Lengths are in meters, areas in square meters and volumes in cubic meters.

composites.description: The quantities per building material, in the order Archicad reports them: one item for each skin of a composite or complex profile element, and a single item for a basic element. Empty for Zones and Morphs, for which Archicad reports no skins.

projectedArea.description: Projected area of the skin. Archicad reports 0 when the legacy intersection and surface calculation is turned on in the Project Preferences.

isCore.description: The skin is marked as core.

isFinish.description: The skin is marked as finish.

subElementId.description: The sub-element (for example a column or beam segment) the skin belongs to. Present only when Archicad attaches the skin to a sub-element.

commands.name: TriangulatePolygonsOfElements
commands.description: Triangulates the plan polygon of the given elements, holes excluded, as Archicad does it: the outline of a Slab, Zone, Hatch or Mesh and the polygon of a Roof. Each triangle is given by the 2D coordinates of its three vertices. The output is aligned with the input array of elements; an element of another type gets an error item.

triangulations.description: The triangulation of the polygon of each element, aligned with the input: its triangles, or an error (for example for an element type that has no polygon).

triangles.description: The triangles covering the polygon of the element, holes excluded, as Archicad triangulates it.

vertices.description: The 2D coordinates of the three vertices of the triangle.

commands.name: GetSurfaceQuantitiesOfElements
commands.description: Gets the exposed surface areas of the given elements calculated by Archicad: for each element one item per surface attribute and building material pair with the area that is not covered by the covering elements (for example the wall area behind a slab is taken off the wall's surface). The covering elements are the optional coverElements; by default every construction element of the project. The output is aligned with the input array of elements.

elements.description: The elements to get the surface quantities of.

coverElements.description: Optional covering elements: the area where one of them overlaps a surface of an element is subtracted from that surface, so for example a slab on a wall takes its footprint off the top surface of the wall. When omitted, every Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Mesh, Stair and Curtain Wall of the project is a covering element. Pass an empty array to get the whole surfaces with nothing subtracted. An element never covers itself.

surfaceQuantitiesOfElements.description: The surface quantities of the elements, in the order of the given elements. Areas are in square meters.

surfaces.description: The surfaces of the element as Archicad reports them: one item per surface attribute and building material pair of the element, so an element has as many items as it has distinct pairs (a basic wall with three different surfaces reports three items). Empty when Archicad reports no surface for the element, for example for an element without a 3D model.

surfaceId.description: The surface (material) attribute of the surface. Left out when the surface is not a project attribute, for example one defined by a GDL script.

buildingMaterialId.description: The building material of the part of the element the surface belongs to.

exposedArea.description: The area of the surface that is not covered by any of the covering elements, in square meters.

commands.name: GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements
commands.description: Gets the subelements of the given hierarchical elements. From Archicad 28 the subelements of external hierarchical elements (for example MEP elements or elements of other add-ons) are returned as externalSubelements.

items.description: Subelements grouped by type.

externalSubelements.description: The subelements of an external hierarchical element (for example an MEP element or an element of another add-on). Available from Archicad 28.

commands.name: GetHierarchicalElementOwners
commands.description: Gets the owner of each given element in its hierarchical element: the root (e.g. the Curtain Wall, Stair or Railing of a frame, tread or post) or the immediate parent. Also returns whether the given element is a main element, a subelement or not part of a hierarchical element.

elements.description: The elements whose owners are looked up, e.g. Curtain Wall frames or panels, Stair treads or Railing posts.

ownerMode.description: root (default): the root of the hierarchical element tree, e.g. the Curtain Wall, Stair or Railing. parent: the immediate parent, which may itself be a subelement.

owners.description: The owner of each element, aligned with the input.

ownerElementId.description: The owner element. For a main element (e.g. a Curtain Wall) or an element that is not part of a hierarchical element, Archicad returns the input element itself.

hierarchicalElementType.description: The classification of the input element (not of its owner): MainElement is the main element of a hierarchical element (e.g. a Curtain Wall, Stair or Railing), ChildElement is a subelement of one (e.g. a frame or a tread), SingleElement is not part of a hierarchical element.

commands.name: GetConnectedElements
commands.description: Gets the elements hosted by (connected to) the given owner elements, filtered to the given element type: for example the Windows or Doors of a Wall, the frames, panels, junctions and accessories of a Curtain Wall, the risers, treads and structures of a Stair, or the posts, rails and panels of a Railing.

elements.description: The owner (host) elements whose connected elements are collected, e.g. Walls, Curtain Walls, Stairs or Railings.

connectedElementType.description: The type of the connected elements to collect, e.g. Window or Door for a Wall owner, or a subelement type of a Curtain Wall, Stair or Railing owner.

commands.name: GetElementsInDrawOrder
commands.description: Returns the identifier of every element of the current database, or of the given databases, in Archicad's drawing order (the order set by Bring to Front and Send to Back), as ACAPI_DrawOrder_DrawOrderGetNext walks it. Use the optional elementType and filters parameters for filtering. Objects that belong to another element (zone stamps, the parts of stairs and railings) are left out unless the IncludeSubElemObjects filter is given.

elementType.description: Optional. Only elements of this type are returned, still in drawing order. If omitted, every element is returned.

filters.description: Optional. The filters an element must pass to be returned, the same as for GetElementsByType.

databases.description: The databases to list the elements of, each in its own drawing order. If omitted, the current database is used.

commands.name: GetSectionElements
commands.description: Gets the elements drawn in the given section, elevation or interior elevation databases, each with the owner element it was generated from. This is the only command that returns raw section element identifiers - every other listing command converts them to their owner - so it is the way to obtain the sectionElementId that CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection requires.

databases.description: The section, elevation or interior elevation databases to list the section elements of. If omitted, the current database is used.

sectionElements.description: The elements drawn in the given databases, each with the owner element it was generated from.

sectionElementId.description: The identifier of the section element itself, accepted by CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection as sectionElementId.

ownerElementId.description: The identifier of the owner element the section element was generated from - this is what every other listing command returns.

ownerElementType.description: The type of the owner element. Only present when the owner's header is readable from the section database.

commands.name: GetRelationsOfElements
commands.description: Gets the type-specific relations of the given elements: endpoint and reference line connections of walls, beams and beam segments, boundary elements and boundary sections of zones, the zones on the two sides of windows, doors, skylights and curtain wall panels, and the zones connected to roofs and shells. Available from Archicad 26.

otherElementType.description: Optional filter: only relations to elements of this type are returned.

relations.description: Type-specific relations of each element, aligned with the input.

commands.name: LinkElements
commands.description: Creates persistent links between pairs of elements, each from one element to another, with an optional integer flags value per link. Scripts can record their own relations between elements this way (for example which label documents which column) instead of storing GUIDs in properties. The links are stored in the project and have no effect on geometry; they are independent from groups, hotlinks and solid element operations. A link is directional: it is returned by GetLinksOfElements for the element it starts from only, and removed by UnlinkElements. Undoable.

links.description: The links to create, each from one element to another.

executionResults.description: One result per link, aligned with the input.

commands.name: UnlinkElements
commands.description: Removes the links created by LinkElements between the given pairs of elements. The direction matters: the link starting from fromElementId and pointing to toElementId is removed. Undoable.

links.description: The links to remove, each from one element to another.

executionResults.description: One result per link, aligned with the input.

commands.name: GetLinksOfElements
commands.description: Gets the links created by LinkElements that start from the given elements: the linked element and the flags of each link. Links pointing to an element are not returned; query the elements they start from. Returns an error item for an element that does not exist.

elements.description: The elements whose outgoing links are returned.

linksOfElements.description: The links starting from each element, aligned with the input.

commands.name: GetZoneBoundaries
commands.description: Gets the boundaries of the given Zones (connected elements, neighbour zones, etc.). Accepts either a single zoneElementId or a list of zones. Prefer the list: the expensive boundary recalculation runs once per call, so querying many Zones in one call is much faster than calling the command once per Zone.

zoneElementId.description: The identifier of a single Zone. Prefer the zones array: querying many Zones in one call is much faster than one call per Zone.

zones.description: A list of Zones. Only one of zoneElementId and zones can be given.

commands.name: GetZoneReductions
commands.description: Gets the area reductions of the given Zones, as the Zone Stamp's area calculation uses them: the polygons of the Zone covered by Walls, Columns, reducing Fills, sloping Roofs and low ceilings, each with its type, the percentage it is reduced by, its area and its outline with holes. Area calculations by local standards need these parts, which GetQuantitiesOfElements only gives as totals. The output is aligned with the input array of elements.

elements.description: A list of Zones.

reductionsOfZones.description: The area reductions of each Zone, aligned with the input array of elements, or an error.

reductions.description: The reduction polygons of the Zone, as its Zone Stamp's area calculation uses them: the parts of the Zone polygon covered by Walls, Columns and reducing Fills, and the parts under a low ceiling (for example under a sloping Roof), each with the percentage it is reduced by and its area. Empty when nothing reduces the Zone's area.

type.description: What reduces the area in the polygon, as the DevKit's APIRoomReduction type of the polygon: Wall, Column, Hatch (a Fill set to reduce the Zone area), Gable (a low ceiling, for example the part under a sloping Roof below the low ceiling height), or Rest (the remaining polygon of the Zone). Unknown for a value this version of Tapir does not name.

percent.description: The percentage by which the area of the polygon reduces the Zone area, as the DevKit reports it.

area.description: The area of the polygon in square meters.

polygonOutline.description: The 2D coordinates of the outline of the polygon in meters; the last coordinate repeats the first.

polygonArcs.description: The arcs of the outline, indices into polygonOutline. Absent when the outline has no arc.

commands.name: UpdateZones
commands.description: Updates all Zones (recalculates their geometry, updates their Zone Stamps and the connected elements).

keepStampPosition.description: Keep the position of the Zone Stamps. The default is true.

undoTopTrim.description: Undo the trimming of the top of the Zones. The default is false.

undoBottomTrim.description: Undo the trimming of the bottom of the Zones. The default is false.

commands.name: SetZoneLabelingSettings
commands.description: Turns the automatic labeling of Zones on or off. Available from Archicad 28.

automaticLabeling.description: Turns the automatic labeling of Zones (placing a Label on each new Zone) on or off.

commands.name: GetCollisions
commands.description: Detect collisions between the given two groups of elements.

volumeTolerance.description: Intersection body volume greater then this value will be considered as a collision. Default value is 0.001.

performSurfaceCheck.description: Enables surface collision check. If disabled the surfaceTolerance value will be ignored. By default it's false.

surfaceTolerance.description: Intersection body surface area greater then this value will be considered as a collision. Default value is 0.001.

commands.name: HighlightElements
commands.description: Highlights the elements given in the elements array. In case of empty elements array removes all previously set highlights.

highlightedColors.description: A list of colors to highlight elements.

items.description: Color of the highlighted element as an [r, g, b, a] array. Each component must be in the 0-255 range.

wireframe3D.description: Optional parameter. Switch non highlighted elements in the 3D window to wireframe.

nonHighlightedColor.description: Optional parameter. Color of the non highlighted elements as an [r, g, b, a] array. Each component must be in the 0-255 range.

commands.name: MoveElements
commands.description: Moves elements with a given vector. An element that cannot be edited (its layer is hidden or locked, it is locked, or it is not available in teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming the reason instead of being skipped silently.

elementsWithMoveVectors.description: The elements with move vector pairs.

copy.description: Optional parameter. If true, then a copy of the element will be moved. By default it's false.

commands.name: RotateElements
commands.description: Rotates elements around a reference point. An element that cannot be edited (its layer is hidden or locked, it is locked, or it is not available in teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming the reason instead of being skipped silently.

beginPoint.description: Starting point of the rotation arc.

endPoint.description: End point of the rotation arc.

copy.description: Optional parameter. If true, a copy of the element is rotated. By default it's false.

commands.name: MirrorElements
commands.description: Mirrors elements across an axis given by two points on the floor plan, optionally as a copy. An element that cannot be edited (its layer is hidden or locked, it is locked, or it is not available in teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming the reason instead of being skipped silently.

mirrorAxis.description: The mirror axis: the line through two points on the floor plan.

beginPoint.description: First point of the mirror axis.

endPoint.description: Second point of the mirror axis. Must differ from beginPoint.

copy.description: Optional parameter. If true, a mirrored copy of the element is created and the original is kept. By default it's false.

commands.name: DeleteElements
commands.description: Deletes elements. The zones of the call are deleted before all the other elements, so an automatic zone deleted together with its bounding walls is gone before its boundary is; deleting the boundary of an automatic zone without the zone itself can open Archicad's modal 'No closed polygon found' dialog, which blocks the command until someone clicks it in Archicad. Returns an execution result for each input element: an element that could not be deleted (for example because its layer is locked) gets a failed execution result instead of being skipped silently.

elements.description: The elements to delete. The zones among them are deleted before all the others, so an automatic zone deleted together with its bounding elements is gone before its boundary is. Deleting the boundary of an automatic zone without the zone itself can open Archicad's modal 'No closed polygon found around the clicked point' dialog, which blocks the command until someone clicks it in Archicad.

commands.name: DeleteSelectedElements
commands.description: Deletes the currently selected elements in one undo step, the same as pressing the Delete key.

commands.name: LockElements
commands.description: Locks the given elements. Manual lock, not teamwork!

commands.name: UnlockElements
commands.description: Unlocks the given elements. Manual lock, not teamwork!

commands.name: GetGDLParametersOfElements
commands.description: Gets all the GDL parameters (name, type, value) of the given elements.

commands.name: SetGDLParametersOfElements
commands.description: Sets the given GDL parameters of the given elements. An element Archicad does not let the user edit (its layer locked, the element locked, or not reserved by the user in Teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming that reason, whatever the parameter.

elementsWithGDLParameters.description: The elements with GDL parameters dictionary pairs.

commands.name: GetMarkerParametersOfElements
commands.description: Gets the marker library part and the marker's GDL parameters (name, type, value) of the given Window and Door elements. The marker is the stamp drawn next to the opening on the floor plan; its parameters are separate from the opening's own GDL parameters, which GetGDLParametersOfElements returns.

markerParametersOfElements.description: The marker of each given element, in the order of the input, or an error for an element that is not a window or a door.

libPart.description: The library part of the marker. Absent when it could not be read.

parameters.description: The GDL parameters of the marker.

commands.name: SetMarkerParametersOfElements
commands.description: Sets the given GDL parameters of the marker of the given Window and Door elements. The opening's own settings and the other marker parameters are left as they are.

elementsWithMarkerParameters.description: The elements with the marker parameters to change.

markerParameters.description: The marker parameters to change, each given by name or by index. The other marker parameters and the opening's own settings are left as they are.

name.description: The name of the marker parameter.

value.description: The new value of the marker parameter: a number for the numeric types (Integer, Length, Angle, RealNumber, PenColor, LineType, Material, FillPattern, BuildingMaterial, Profile, RGBColor, Intensity), a string for String and Title, true/false for Boolean and 'On'/'Off' for LightSwitch. Array parameters are not supported.

index.description: The index of the marker parameter, as GetMarkerParametersOfElements reports it.

value.description: The new value of the marker parameter, see the value given with a name.

commands.name: RunParameterScriptOfElements
commands.description: Runs the parameter script of the library part of the given elements (objects, lamps, windows, doors, etc.), so that parameter values that depend on other parameters are updated, e.g. after SetGDLParametersOfElements.

commands.name: CreateColumns
commands.description: Creates Column elements based on the given parameters.

columnsData.description: Array of data to create Columns.

items.description: The parameters of the new Column.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

height.description: Optional column height.

axisRotationAngle.description: Optional column rotation angle in radians.

slantAngle.description: Optional slant angle in radians. A non-zero value also makes the column slanted, unless isSlanted is given explicitly.

isSlanted.description: Optional explicit slanted state. By default it is derived from slantAngle.

slantDirectionAngle.description: Optional rotation angle of the slanted column on the horizontal plane in radians.

width.description: Cross section width of the column. Applied to all segments.

depth.description: Cross section depth (height) of the column. Applied to all segments. Only effective for rectangular columns.

circleBased.description: True for a round column cross section, false for rectangular. Ignored if profileId is also given. Applied to all segments.

isWidthAndHeightLinked.description: When true (the default), Archicad keeps width and depth equal and setting one changes the other - set to false to give width/depth independent values. Applied to all segments.

buildingMaterialId.description: Cross section building material (round or rectangular, per circleBased). Applied to all segments.

profileId.description: Switches the cross section to this custom extruded profile (circleBased becomes false). Applied to all segments.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from the coordinate's z value.

commands.name: CreateWalls
commands.description: Creates Wall elements based on the given parameters.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a Wall favorite to base the new element on. Its settings (structure, reference line location, top link, offsets, ...) are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them. With a favorite only begCoordinate and endCoordinate are needed.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

floorIndex.description: Story index (as returned by GetStories). When provided, zCoordinate is interpreted as bottomOffset relative to the floor. Takes priority over zCoordinate for floor assignment.

zCoordinate.description: Absolute Z when floorIndex is absent; bottomOffset relative to the floor when floorIndex is provided.

height.description: Optional explicit height. Sets relativeTopStory to 0, so it replaces the top link of the favorite or the tool default. When omitted, the height and top link of the favorite (or of the Wall tool defaults) are kept.

thickness.description: Optional thickness. When omitted, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's thickness is kept. Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) wall - a Composite or Profile wall takes its thickness from the composite or profile attribute. Without structureType the new wall keeps the structure of the favorite (or the wall tool default), which may be a composite; send structureType 'Basic' for the thickness to apply.

offset.description: Optional reference line offset. When omitted, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's offset is kept.

arcAngle.description: Arc angle in radians; non-zero creates a curved wall (begCoordinate/endCoordinate are the chord endpoints).

referenceLineLocation.description: Optional. When omitted, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's reference line location is kept. The Core* values only have an effect on a Composite or Profile wall.

structureType.description: Optional. When neither this nor one of the attribute ids below is given, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's structure is kept.

contourPen.description: Pen of the wall's own contour/reference outline (API_WallType::contPen) - distinct from cutFillPen, which is the cut fill pattern's pen.

contourPen3D.description: Pen of the wall's contour in 3D views (API_WallType::contPen3D).

contourLineTypeId.description: Line type of the wall's own contour (API_WallType::contLtype) - pairs with contourPen, which only sets the pen, not the line type.

belowViewLineTypeId.description: Line type used when "OutLines Only" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup (API_WallType::belowViewLineType).

aboveViewLinePen.description: Pen used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup.

aboveViewLineTypeId.description: Line type used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup - pairs with aboveViewLinePen.

viewDepthLimitation.description: Only has an effect on a multi-story wall (relativeTopStory/topOffset making it span more than one story).

useCompositePriority.description: When true, the Composite's own priority is used at junctions instead of connectionPriority.

linkToSettings.description: When newCreationMode is true, homeStoryDifference overrides the home story selected by floorIndex or derived from zCoordinate.

inheritEndSurface.description: The end surface of the wall is inherited from the adjoining wall.

alignTexture.description: Align texture mapping to the wall's edges.

polyCanChange.description: The polygonal wall's corners can be changed in case of L and T connections. Only meaningful for a Polygonal wall (geometryType).

materialsChained.description: Whether the surface materials are chained.

logHeight.description: Height of the log for log walls. 0 means a normal (non-log) wall.

commands.name: CreateBeams
commands.description: Creates Beam elements based on the given parameters.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from zCoordinate.

slantAngle.description: Slant angle in radians. A non-zero value also switches the beam to slanted, unless isSlanted is given explicitly.

isSlanted.description: Optional explicit slanted state. By default it is derived from slantAngle.

profileAngle.description: Rotation angle of the profile around the beam's center line, in radians.

arcAngle.description: Optional arc angle in radians. A non-zero value makes a horizontally curved beam.

verticalCurveHeight.description: Optional rise of a vertically curved beam. A non-zero value makes a vertically curved beam; it wins over arcAngle.

width.description: Cross section width of the beam. Applied to all segments.

height.description: Cross section height of the beam. Applied to all segments.

circleBased.description: True for a round beam cross section, false for rectangular. Ignored if profileId is also given. Applied to all segments.

isWidthAndHeightLinked.description: When true (the default), Archicad keeps width and height equal and setting one changes the other - set to false to give width/height independent values. Applied to all segments.

buildingMaterialId.description: Cross section building material (round or rectangular, per circleBased). Applied to all segments.

profileId.description: Switches the cross section to this custom extruded profile (circleBased becomes false). Applied to all segments.

commands.name: CreateStairs
commands.description: Creates Stair elements based on the given baseline and parameters.

stairsData.description: Array of data to create Stair elements.

items.description: The parameters of the new Stair.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

baseLinePoints.description: 2D coordinates defining the stair baseline polyline. Minimum 2 points for a straight stair, 3+ for L-shaped or U-shaped stairs.

zCoordinate.description: The Z coordinate (absolute elevation) of the stair base.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from zCoordinate.

finishVisible.description: Optional. If false, the tread/riser finishes are hidden and only the stair structure (e.g. a monolith) is modeled.

commands.name: SolveStairBaseline
commands.description: Runs the Archicad stair solver on the given Stair baselines and parameters without creating any element. Returns for each one whether the baseline was already correct, could be solved or could not be solved, with the baseline and the main stair settings after solving. Available from Archicad 27.

stairsData.description: Array of Stair data to check, with the same fields as the items of CreateStairs (without favoriteName). Nothing is created.

items.description: The parameters of the Stair to check. Fields that are not given come from the current Stair tool defaults, as in CreateStairs.

baseLinePoints.description: 2D coordinates defining the stair baseline polyline. Minimum 2 points for a straight stair, 3+ for L-shaped or U-shaped stairs.

zCoordinate.description: The Z coordinate (absolute elevation) of the stair base.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from zCoordinate.

finishVisible.description: Optional. If false, the tread/riser finishes are hidden and only the stair structure (e.g. a monolith) is modeled.

solutions.description: The results of the stair solver, aligned with the input stairsData.

solution.description: Correct: the baseline was already valid, nothing changed. Solved: the solver turned it into a valid baseline, returned in baseLinePoints. NotSolved: no valid baseline was found; CreateStairs is likely to fail or create an invalid stair with this input.

baseLinePoints.description: The baseline polyline after the solver ran.

baseLineArcs.description: The arcs of the baseline after the solver ran, indexing baseLinePoints. Present only when the baseline has arcs.

totalHeight.description: Total height of the stair after the solver ran.

flightWidth.description: Width of the stair flight after the solver ran.

stepNum.description: Number of risers after the solver ran.

riserHeight.description: Height of each riser after the solver ran.

treadDepth.description: Depth (going) of each tread after the solver ran.

commands.name: CreateSlabs
commands.description: Creates Slab elements based on the given parameters.

slabsData.description: Array of data to create Slabs.

items.description: The parameters of the new Slab.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

level.description: The Z coordinate value of the reference line of the slab.

thickness.description: Optional slab thickness. Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) slab - a Composite slab takes its thickness from the composite attribute. Without structureType, buildingMaterialId or compositeId the new slab keeps the structure of the slab tool default (or the favorite), which may be a composite; send structureType 'Basic' for the thickness to apply.

structureType.description: Optional structure of the slab. If omitted, derived from buildingMaterialId or compositeId when one is given, otherwise the slab tool default (or the favorite) is kept.

buildingMaterialId.description: Building material of a Basic slab. Cannot be combined with compositeId.

compositeId.description: Composite attribute of a Composite slab. Cannot be combined with buildingMaterialId.

referencePlaneLocation.description: For a basic (homogeneous) slab only 'Top' or 'Bottom' are valid.

polygonCoordinates.description: The 2D coordinates of the edge of the slab.

polygonArcs.description: Polygon outline arcs of the slab.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from level.

commands.name: CreateWindows
commands.description: Creates Window elements in host walls based on the given parameters.

libraryPartName.description: Optional. Localized library part name (docu_UName) to place instead of the tool default/favorite, e.g. a shutter part that has no favorite. It has to be a window library part. Applied to the tool defaults before cloning.

favoriteName.description: Optional. Name of an existing Window favorite (as returned by `GetFavoritesByType`). Applied to the Window tool defaults before the create.

commands.name: CreateDoors
commands.description: Creates Door elements in host walls based on the given parameters.

libraryPartName.description: Optional. Localized library part name (docu_UName) to place instead of the tool default/favorite, e.g. a shutter part that has no favorite. It has to be a door library part. Applied to the tool defaults before cloning.

favoriteName.description: Optional. Name of an existing Door favorite (as returned by `GetFavoritesByType`). Applied to the Door tool defaults before the create.

commands.name: CreateOpenings
commands.description: Creates Opening elements in the given host elements.

commands.name: GetOpeningDefault
commands.description: Returns the settings of the Opening tool defaults: the extrusion parameters (as GetOpeningDetails returns them) and the floor plan parameters (as GetOpeningFloorPlanParameters returns them). Available from Archicad 29.

extrusionParameters.description: The size and extrusion settings. A size Archicad does not give for the opening's shape is left out.

anchor.description: The anchor point of the opening's polygon.

extrusionSurfaceId.description: The surface of the extrusion faces. Only given when it is overridden.

endSurfaceId.description: The surface of the end faces. Only given when it is overridden.

showReferenceAxis.description: Whether the reference axis of the opening is shown on the floor plan.

referenceAxisLineTypeId.description: The line type of the reference axis.

referenceAxisOverhang.description: How far the reference axis reaches beyond the opening.

cutSurfacesUseLineOfCutElements.description: Whether the cut surfaces use the line of the cut elements instead of cutSurfacesLinePen and cutSurfacesLineTypeId.

outlinesUseLineOfCutElements.description: Whether the outlines use the line of the cut elements instead of the uncut and overhead lines below.

coverFillsUseFillsOfCutElements.description: Whether the cover fills are the fills of the cut elements instead of coverFillId.

coverFillId.description: The fill of the cover fills.

coverFillTransformation.description: The orientation and distortion of the cover fill. Left out when Archicad gives none.

cutSymbolLibPartId.description: The id of the library part drawn as the symbol of the cut opening. Left out when the opening has no cut symbol.

unCutSymbolLibPartId.description: The id of the library part drawn as the symbol of the uncut opening. Left out when the opening has no uncut symbol.

commands.name: GetOpeningFloorPlanParameters
commands.description: Returns the floor plan parameters of Opening elements: the reference axis, the cut surface and outline lines, the cover fills and the cut and uncut symbols. Available from Archicad 29.

elements.description: The Opening elements (made with the Opening tool) to read.

openings.description: The floor plan parameters of the openings, in the order of the given elements.

showReferenceAxis.description: Whether the reference axis of the opening is shown on the floor plan.

referenceAxisLineTypeId.description: The line type of the reference axis.

referenceAxisOverhang.description: How far the reference axis reaches beyond the opening.

cutSurfacesUseLineOfCutElements.description: Whether the cut surfaces use the line of the cut elements instead of cutSurfacesLinePen and cutSurfacesLineTypeId.

outlinesUseLineOfCutElements.description: Whether the outlines use the line of the cut elements instead of the uncut and overhead lines below.

coverFillsUseFillsOfCutElements.description: Whether the cover fills are the fills of the cut elements instead of coverFillId.

coverFillId.description: The fill of the cover fills.

coverFillTransformation.description: The orientation and distortion of the cover fill. Left out when Archicad gives none.

cutSymbolLibPartId.description: The id of the library part drawn as the symbol of the cut opening. Left out when the opening has no cut symbol.

unCutSymbolLibPartId.description: The id of the library part drawn as the symbol of the uncut opening. Left out when the opening has no uncut symbol.

commands.name: SetOpeningFloorPlanParameters
commands.description: Changes the floor plan parameters of Opening elements returned by GetOpeningFloorPlanParameters, and sets or removes their cut and uncut symbols. Available from Archicad 29.

floorPlanParameters.description: The floor plan parameters to change, with the names GetOpeningFloorPlanParameters returns. The ones left out are not changed.

showReferenceAxis.description: Whether the reference axis of the opening is shown on the floor plan.

referenceAxisLineTypeId.description: The line type of the reference axis.

referenceAxisOverhang.description: How far the reference axis reaches beyond the opening.

cutSurfacesUseLineOfCutElements.description: Whether the cut surfaces use the line of the cut elements instead of cutSurfacesLinePen and cutSurfacesLineTypeId.

outlinesUseLineOfCutElements.description: Whether the outlines use the line of the cut elements instead of the uncut and overhead lines below.

coverFillsUseFillsOfCutElements.description: Whether the cover fills are the fills of the cut elements instead of coverFillId.

coverFillId.description: The fill of the cover fills.

coverFillTransformation.description: The orientation and distortion of the cover fill. Left out when Archicad gives none.

cutSymbolLibPartId.description: The id of the library part drawn as the symbol of the cut opening. Left out when the opening has no cut symbol.

unCutSymbolLibPartId.description: The id of the library part drawn as the symbol of the uncut opening. Left out when the opening has no uncut symbol.

clearCutSymbol.description: Removes the cut symbol of the opening. Cannot be given together with cutSymbolLibPartId.

clearUnCutSymbol.description: Removes the uncut symbol of the opening. Cannot be given together with unCutSymbolLibPartId.

commands.name: GetOpeningDetails
commands.description: Returns the details of Opening elements: the parent element, the cut and connected elements, the geometry (anchor point, extrusion direction, axes, polygon) and the extrusion parameters (size, anchor, offsets, surface overrides). Available from Archicad 29.

elements.description: The Opening elements (made with the Opening tool) to read.

openings.description: The details of the openings, in the order of the given elements.

parentElementId.description: The element the opening was placed in. Left out when the opening has none.

connectedOpenings.description: The openings Archicad reports as connected to this one. Left out when they cannot be read.

anchorPoint.description: The anchor point of the opening in world coordinates.

extrusionDirection.description: The direction the opening is extruded in.

xAxis.description: The X axis of the plane of the opening's polygon.

yAxis.description: The Y axis of the plane of the opening's polygon.

polygon.description: The vertices of the opening's polygon, in the plane of xAxis and yAxis. Left out when the opening has no polygon.

extrusionParameters.description: The size and extrusion settings. A size Archicad does not give for the opening's shape is left out.

anchor.description: The anchor point of the opening's polygon.

extrusionSurfaceId.description: The surface of the extrusion faces. Only given when it is overridden.

endSurfaceId.description: The surface of the end faces. Only given when it is overridden.

commands.name: SetOpeningDetails
commands.description: Changes the details of Opening elements: the parent element, the cut elements, the polygon, a transformation of the geometry and the extrusion parameters (size, anchor, offsets, surface overrides) returned by GetOpeningDetails. Available from Archicad 29.

openingsWithDetails.description: The Opening elements (made with the Opening tool) to change, each with the details to set. A detail that is left out stays as it is.

parentElementId.description: The new element the opening belongs to.

addCutElements.description: Elements the opening should cut as well.

removeCutElements.description: Elements the opening should no longer cut.

polygon.description: The new polygon of the opening, in the plane of the xAxis and yAxis returned by GetOpeningDetails.

transformation.description: A transformation applied to the opening's geometry: a 3x4 matrix of 12 numbers, row by row, the 4th, 8th and 12th numbers being the translation along X, Y and Z. For example [1,0,0,1, 0,1,0,0, 0,0,1,0] moves the opening by 1 along X.

extrusionParameters.description: The size and extrusion settings to change, with the same names GetOpeningDetails returns.

anchor.description: The anchor point of the opening's polygon.

extrusionSurfaceId.description: The surface of the extrusion faces. Only used when the surface is overridden.

endSurfaceId.description: The surface of the end faces. Only used when the surface is overridden.

commands.name: CreateMorphs
commands.description: Creates Morph elements from simple box definitions.

size.description: Builds a simple axis-aligned box of this size. Mutually exclusive with `body` - give exactly one of the two.

body.description: Builds arbitrary geometry instead of a simple box. Mutually exclusive with `size` - give exactly one of the two.

topExpansion.description: Only used with `size` (box) morphs. Expands the top rectangle outwards on all four sides by this amount, creating a frustum (e.g. sloped excavation shape). 0 creates a cuboid.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from the basePoint's z value.

commands.name: CreateRoofs
commands.description: Creates Roof elements based on footprint, level and roof profile data. Creates a multi-plane roof by default; pass 'pivotLine' (and optionally 'angle') to create a single-plane roof instead.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from level.

thickness.description: Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) roof - a Composite roof takes its thickness from the composite attribute. Without structureType the new roof keeps the structure of the roof tool default (or the favorite), which may be a composite; send structureType 'Basic' for the thickness to apply.

pivotLine.description: If given, creates a single-plane roof instead of a multi-plane roof, tilted along this pivot line.

angle.description: Slope angle of the single-plane roof in radians. Only valid together with 'pivotLine'.

commands.name: CreateCurtainWalls
commands.description: Creates Curtain Wall elements along a reference polyline with a column (primary) and row (secondary) pattern. The frame and panel classes come from the favorite or from the Curtain Wall tool defaults; the pattern cells can assign them to the grid.

curtainWallsData.description: Array of data to create Curtain Walls.

items.description: The parameters of the new Curtain Wall. Everything not given here - the frame and panel classes, the surfaces, the boundary and corner frames, the pattern - comes from the favorite or from the Curtain Wall tool defaults of the open project.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

coordinates.description: The 2D coordinates of the reference line of the curtain wall on the floor plan. Each pair of consecutive coordinates becomes one straight segment, so two coordinates give a single-segment curtain wall.

zCoordinate.description: Optional Z coordinate (absolute elevation) of the bottom of the curtain wall. When omitted, the base level of the favorite (or of the Curtain Wall tool defaults) relative to the floor is kept.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. When omitted, derived from zCoordinate if that is given, otherwise the current story.

height.description: Optional height of the curtain wall. When omitted, the height of the favorite (or of the Curtain Wall tool defaults) is kept.

primaryPattern.description: Optional column pattern: the sizes of the columns along the segment (the primary grid). When omitted, the pattern of the favorite (or of the tool defaults) is kept.

secondaryPattern.description: Optional row pattern: the sizes of the rows from the bottom up (the secondary grid). When omitted, the pattern of the favorite (or of the tool defaults) is kept.

cells.description: Optional assignment of panel and frame classes to the cells of the pattern unit. The unit repeats along and up the segment, so an assignment applies to every repetition of that cell. A cell not listed here keeps the assignment of the favorite (or of the tool defaults) when the pattern is unchanged, otherwise the assignment of the first default cell.

commands.name: CreateAssociativeDimensions
commands.description: Creates associative linear dimensions from explicit witness point references. A witness point can also be static, given by its coordinate instead of an element.

commands.name: CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection
commands.description: Creates associative linear dimensions on section elements using common wall, slab, beam, column and opening presets. The preset points of multiple section elements can be merged into one continuous dimension chain via sectionElementIds.

sectionElementId.description: The identifier of a single section element. Only one of sectionElementId and sectionElementIds can be given.

sectionElementIds.description: A list of section elements whose preset points are merged into one continuous dimension chain. Only one of sectionElementId and sectionElementIds can be given.

commands.name: CreateWallThicknessDimensions
commands.description: Creates associative wall thickness dimensions for the given walls.

commands.name: GetDimensionData
commands.description: Gets witness point data (coordinates, measured values) from existing dimension chains.

elements.description: The identifier of the dimension elements.

commands.name: GetOpeningTransformations
commands.description: Gets the placement of Opening elements without changing them: the global-to-local transformation matrix Archicad returns, its inverse, and the origin and axes of the opening in world coordinates derived from the inverse. Mirrored openings give a left-handed matrix (isMirrored). Needs Archicad 27 or later.

openingTransformations.description: The transformation of each given Opening, or an error, in the order of the input elements.

globalToLocal.description: The matrix as Archicad returns it (API_Tranmat, global to local): the 12 values of a 3x4 matrix, row by row, so x' = m[0]*x + m[1]*y + m[2]*z + m[3], y' = m[4]*x + ... + m[7], z' = m[8]*x + ... + m[11].

localToGlobal.description: The inverse of globalToLocal, in the same layout. Missing when globalToLocal cannot be inverted.

origin.description: The origin of the opening's local coordinate system in world coordinates, from localToGlobal. Missing when globalToLocal cannot be inverted.

xAxis.description: The local X axis in world coordinates, from localToGlobal. Missing when globalToLocal cannot be inverted.

yAxis.description: The local Y axis in world coordinates, from localToGlobal. Missing when globalToLocal cannot be inverted.

zAxis.description: The local Z axis in world coordinates, from localToGlobal. Missing when globalToLocal cannot be inverted.

determinant.description: The determinant of the 3x3 part of globalToLocal. Zero (or nearly) when it cannot be inverted.

isMirrored.description: True when the matrix is left-handed (negative determinant), which Archicad returns for a mirrored opening.

commands.name: CreateZones
commands.description: Creates Zone elements based on the given parameters.

zonesData.description: Array of data to create Zones.

items.description: The parameters of the new Zone.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

floorIndex.description: Optional story index of the new zone. An automatic zone (geometry.referencePosition) is found around its reference point on this story, which is made active in the floor plan while the zone is created; the previously active story is restored afterwards.

name.description: Name of the zone.

categoryAttributeId.description: The identifier of the zone category attribute.

stampPosition.description: Position of the origin of the zone stamp.

stampAngle.description: Optional zone stamp rotation angle in radians.

fixedStampAngle.description: If true, the zone stamp angle remains fixed when the element is rotated.

commands.name: CreatePolylines
commands.description: Creates Polyline elements based on the given parameters.

polylinesData.description: Array of data to create Polylines.

items.description: The parameters of the new Polyline.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

floorInd.description: The identifier of the floor. Optional parameter, by default the current floor is used.

layerIndex.description: Layer attribute index to place the polyline on. Optional parameter, by default the current layer is used.

linePenIndex.description: Pen index of the polyline contour. Optional parameter, by default the current pen is used.

lineTypeIndex.description: Line type attribute index of the polyline contour. Optional parameter, by default the current line type is used.

penWeightMm.description: Optional pen weight override in mm.

roomSeparator.description: Is this a zone boundary line? Optional, defaults to false.

commands.name: CreateLineElements
commands.description: Creates Line elements based on the given parameters.

linesData.description: Array of data to create Lines.

items.description: The parameters of the new Line.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

floorInd.description: The identifier of the floor. Optional parameter, by default the current floor is used.

layerIndex.description: Layer attribute index to place the line on. Optional parameter, by default the current layer is used.

roomSeparator.description: Is this a zone boundary line? Optional, defaults to false.

linePenIndex.description: Optional pen index. By default the current pen is used.

lineTypeId.description: Optional line type attribute. By default the current line type is used.

commands.name: CreateArcs
commands.description: Creates Arc elements based on the given parameters.

arcsData.description: Array of data to create Arcs.

items.description: The parameters of the new Arc.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

floorInd.description: The identifier of the floor. Optional parameter, by default the current floor is used.

layerIndex.description: Layer attribute index to place the arc on. Optional parameter, by default the current layer is used.

begAngle.description: Beginning angle of the arc in radians.

endAngle.description: End angle of the arc in radians.

roomSeparator.description: Is this a zone boundary line? Optional, defaults to false.

linePenIndex.description: Optional pen index. By default the current pen is used.

lineTypeId.description: Optional line type attribute. By default the current line type is used.

commands.name: CreateCircles
commands.description: Creates Circle elements based on the given parameters.

circlesData.description: Array of data to create Circles.

items.description: The parameters of the new Circle.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

floorInd.description: The identifier of the floor. Optional parameter, by default the current floor is used.

layerIndex.description: Layer attribute index to place the circle on. Optional parameter, by default the current layer is used.

roomSeparator.description: Is this a zone boundary line? Optional, defaults to false.

linePenIndex.description: Optional pen index. By default the current pen is used.

lineTypeId.description: Optional line type attribute. By default the current line type is used.

commands.name: CreateHotspots
commands.description: Creates Hotspot elements based on the given parameters.

hotspotsData.description: Array of data to create Hotspots.

items.description: The parameters of the new Hotspot.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

floorInd.description: The identifier of the floor. Optional parameter, by default the current floor is used.

layerIndex.description: Layer attribute index to place the hotspot on. Optional parameter, by default the current layer is used.

penIndex.description: Optional pen index. By default the current pen is used.

commands.name: CreateHatches
commands.description: Creates Hatch elements based on the given parameters.

hatchesData.description: Array of data to create Hatches.

items.description: The parameters of the new Hatch.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

floorInd.description: The identifier of the floor. Optional parameter, by default the current floor is used.

layerIndex.description: Layer attribute index to place the hatch on. Optional parameter, by default the current layer is used.

coordinates.description: The 2D coordinates of the hatch outline (single contour, no holes). Do not repeat the first point at the end.

arcs.description: The arcs of the hatch outline.

contourPenIndex.description: Optional pen index for the contour. By default the current pen is used.

fillPenIndex.description: Optional pen index for the fill. By default the current pen is used.

foregroundColor.description: Optional RGB color (components between 0.0 and 1.0) of the fill foreground, used instead of fillPenIndex. Takes precedence over fillPenIndex when both are given. The same format as the colors returned by GetZoneCategories and GetPenTables.

backgroundColor.description: Optional RGB color (components between 0.0 and 1.0) of the fill background, used instead of fillBackgroundPenIndex. Takes precedence over fillBackgroundPenIndex when both are given.

fillId.description: Optional fill attribute. By default the current fill is used.

roomSpecial.description: Special area percent in a room (negative means OFF).

items.description: The parameters of the new Spline.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

floorInd.description: The identifier of the floor. Optional parameter, by default the current floor is used.

layerIndex.description: Layer attribute index to place the spline on. Optional parameter, by default the current layer is used.

coordinates.description: The 2D coordinates of the spline points. Do not repeat the first point at the end even for a closed spline.

closed.description: Is this a closed curve? Optional, defaults to false.

roomSeparator.description: Is this a zone boundary line? Optional, defaults to false.

linePenIndex.description: Optional pen index. By default the current pen is used.

lineTypeId.description: Optional line type attribute. By default the current line type is used.
