commands.name: GetGridElementDefaults
commands.description: Returns the Grid Tool defaults: library part, size and GDL parameters of a new grid element. Needs Archicad 26 or later.

elementId.description: The grid element. The zero GUID for the tool defaults.

variation.description: Four-character variation of the object: 'GREL' for a grid element.

floorIndex.description: Home story index.

pos.description: Insertion point: the start of the grid line.

angle.description: Direction of the grid line in radians.

length.description: Length of the grid line: the GDL parameter AC_Length of the Grid Tool's grid marker, or the object's A size for a library part without it.

xRatio.description: The object's xRatio as stored: its A size with useXYFixSize on, otherwise the A size divided by the library part's own A.

yRatio.description: The object's yRatio as stored, like xRatio for the B size.

useXYFixSize.description: Whether xRatio and yRatio hold the sizes themselves.

level.description: Elevation of the object from its home story.

libraryPartName.description: Localized name of the library part.

parameters.description: GDL parameters, separators left out. Only when requested.

type.description: Integer, Length, Angle, RealNum, LightSwitch, ColorRGB, Intensity, LineType, Material, FillPattern, PenColor, String, Boolean, Title, BuildingMaterial, Profile, Dictionary or Unknown.

value.description: Number for numeric and boolean types, string for String and Title. Not given for arrays.

dimension1.description: First dimension of an array parameter.

dimension2.description: Second dimension of an array parameter.

commands.name: GetGridElements
commands.description: Lists the grid elements (placed with the Grid Tool or created by CreateGridElements) with their position, angle, size, library part and optionally GDL parameters. Needs Archicad 26 or later.

includeParameters.description: Also return the GDL parameters of each grid element. Default false.

elementId.description: The grid element. The zero GUID for the tool defaults.

variation.description: Four-character variation of the object: 'GREL' for a grid element.

floorIndex.description: Home story index.

pos.description: Insertion point: the start of the grid line.

angle.description: Direction of the grid line in radians.

length.description: Length of the grid line: the GDL parameter AC_Length of the Grid Tool's grid marker, or the object's A size for a library part without it.

xRatio.description: The object's xRatio as stored: its A size with useXYFixSize on, otherwise the A size divided by the library part's own A.

yRatio.description: The object's yRatio as stored, like xRatio for the B size.

useXYFixSize.description: Whether xRatio and yRatio hold the sizes themselves.

level.description: Elevation of the object from its home story.

libraryPartName.description: Localized name of the library part.

parameters.description: GDL parameters, separators left out. Only when requested.

type.description: Integer, Length, Angle, RealNum, LightSwitch, ColorRGB, Intensity, LineType, Material, FillPattern, PenColor, String, Boolean, Title, BuildingMaterial, Profile, Dictionary or Unknown.

value.description: Number for numeric and boolean types, string for String and Title. Not given for arrays.

dimension1.description: First dimension of an array parameter.

dimension2.description: Second dimension of an array parameter.

commands.name: CreateGridElements
commands.description: Creates grid elements, the elements the Grid Tool places, from begin and end coordinates, with optional story, layer and GDL parameters. Needs Archicad 26 or later.

begCoordinate.description: Start point of the grid line (the object's insertion point).

endCoordinate.description: End point of the grid line. Sets the direction and, unless lengthMode is 'none', the length.

lengthMode.description: How the line length is applied. length (default): to the GDL parameter AC_Length when the library part has it, as the Grid Tool's grid marker does; otherwise to the object's A size, converted to xRatio as CreateObjects does. none: the length is left to 'parameters'.

floorIndex.description: Home story index. Default: the tool default.

layerIndex.description: Layer attribute index. Only a positive index takes effect. Default: the tool default.

parameters.description: GDL parameters to set by name (read the names with GetGridElementDefaults). The value is a number, a boolean or a string. Unknown names and wrong value types are reported in warnings and skipped. The tool defaults can look different from a grid drawn with the Grid Tool (for example a short line with a leader to the bubble); to get the same look, copy the parameters of such a grid (GetGridElements with includeParameters).

value.description: A number or a boolean for a numeric parameter, a string for a String or Title parameter.

warnings.description: Parameters that were not set, prefixed with the index of the grid element.

commands.name: CreateMeshes
commands.description: Creates Mesh elements based on the given parameters.

meshesData.description: Array of data to create Meshes.

items.description: The parameters of the new Mesh.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

level.description: The Z reference level of coordinates.

buildingMaterialId.description: Optional building material of the mesh. Its top, side and bottom surface overrides are cleared, also one from the Mesh tool defaults, so the mesh shows the building material's own surface.

showLines.description: Whether to show secondary mesh lines (level lines other than the user-defined ones) on plan.

contourPen.description: Optional pen attribute index for the mesh's contour line.

levelPen.description: Optional pen attribute index for the mesh's level lines.

lineTypeIndex.description: Optional line type attribute index for the mesh's contour.

polygonCoordinates.description: The 3D coordinates of the outline polygon of the mesh.

polygonArcs.description: Polygon outline arcs of the mesh.

sublines.description: The leveling sublines inside the polygon of the mesh.

commands.name: CreateLabels
commands.description: Creates Label elements based on the given parameters.

labelsData.description: Array of data to create Labels.

items.description: The parameters of the new Label.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

parentElementId.description: The parent element if the label is an associative label.

labelClass.description: Optional; if omitted, inherits the current Label tool default (which may silently resolve to either class - explicitly setting this avoids ambiguity). 'Symbol' needs a symbol library part, which only the Label tool default or the favorite given in favoriteName can provide: when those are a Text label, the item fails instead of placing a label without content.

text.description: The text content if the label is a text label. Newlines create multiple lines; Windows-style CRLF (and bare CR) line endings are normalized to LF. Ignored if 'runs' is also given.

runs.description: Multi-style text content for a text label: an array of styled runs, concatenated in order. Takes precedence over 'text' if both are given.

begCoordinate.description: The begin coordinate of leader line. Optional parameter, but either begCoordinate or parentElementId must be provided. Unless midCoordinate and endCoordinate are both given too, the label is created at its default position relative to the parent element (Archicad's 'createAtDefaultPosition'), so the label may not end up at begCoordinate - read it back with GetDetailsOfElements after creation.

midCoordinate.description: The mid coordinate of leader line. Optional parameter; give it together with endCoordinate to place the label exactly where the coordinates say.

endCoordinate.description: The end coordinate of leader line. Optional parameter; give it together with midCoordinate to place the label exactly where the coordinates say.

floorInd.description: The identifier of the floor. Optional parameter, by default the current floor or the floor of the parent element is used.

commands.name: CreateTexts
commands.description: Creates standalone Text elements based on the given parameters.

textsData.description: Array of data to create Texts.

items.description: The parameters of the new Text element.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

coordinate.description: The placement position of the text. The z value is used to determine the floor when floorIndex is omitted.

text.description: The text content. Newlines create multiple lines; Windows-style CRLF (and bare CR) line endings are normalized to LF. Ignored if 'runs' is also given.

runs.description: Multi-style text content: an array of styled runs, concatenated in order. Takes precedence over 'text' if both are given.

height.description: The character height in millimeters. Optional; defaults to the Text tool default. Equivalent to style.height.

pen.description: Optional pen attribute index. Equivalent to style.penIndex.

angle.description: Optional rotation angle in radians. Equivalent to style.angle.

style.description: height/pen/angle/justification above take precedence over the same fields here if both are given.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from the coordinate's z value.

layerIndex.description: Optional layer attribute index. If omitted, the Text tool default layer is used.

commands.name: CreateLevelDimensions
commands.description: Creates Level Dimension elements (the Level Dimension tool) based on the given parameters. With a parentElementId the dimension is associative: it shows the height of the parent element (Mesh, Slab, Roof ...) at its position and follows the element when it changes.

levelDimensionsData.description: Array of data to create Level Dimensions (the Level Dimension tool of the floor plan).

items.description: The parameters of the new Level Dimension.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a Level Dimension favorite to base the new element on. Its settings (marker, format, text style, layer, pen) are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

position.description: The location of the marker on the floor plan. With a parentElementId it must lie on that element, the measured level is the parent's height at this point. Outside the parent's outline Archicad still creates the dimension, but without a height (GetDetailsOfElements reads a level of -110000000).

parentElementId.description: Optional element the level dimension is associated with (Mesh, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Beam, Column, Wall, Object, Stair ...). The dimension then shows the element's height at the position and follows the element when it changes. Without it the dimension measures the floor level, or the given static level.

level.description: Optional fixed level value in meters (absolute, from the project zero). Only used without parentElementId; the dimension then shows this value instead of the floor level.

floorIndex.description: The index of the floor to place the dimension on. Optional parameter, by default the floor of the parent element, otherwise the current floor is used.

layerIndex.description: Layer attribute index to place the dimension on. Optional parameter, by default the layer of the favorite or the Level Dimension tool default is used.

pen.description: Pen index of the marker. Optional parameter.

textHeight.description: Height of the dimension text in millimeters (paper size). Optional parameter.

textPen.description: Pen index of the dimension text. Optional parameter.

dimForm.description: Marker type of the Level Dimension tool, 0-19 as Archicad stores it (read it back with GetDetailsOfElements from an existing level dimension or one placed with a favorite). Optional parameter.

needPlus.description: Show a plus sign for positive values. Optional parameter.

markerSize.description: Size of the marker in millimeters (paper size). Optional parameter.

angle.description: Rotation angle of the marker in radians. Optional parameter.

origin.description: The origin the level is measured from. Optional parameter.

commands.name: ModifyWalls
commands.description: Modifies Wall elements based on the given parameters.

geometryType.description: Polygonal is not settable here; it is read-only via GetDetailsOfElements. This is unrelated to slantAlpha/slantBeta - see profileType for the cross section shape those depend on.

arcAngle.description: Arc angle in radians; non-zero makes the wall curved (begCoordinate/endCoordinate are the chord endpoints).

height.description: Sets relativeTopStory to 0 (explicit height). Do not combine with relativeTopStory in the same call - whichever is applied last wins, and Archicad recomputes the actual height from the story elevations once relativeTopStory is non-zero.

thickness.description: Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) wall - a Composite or Profile wall takes its thickness from the composite or profile attribute. Send structureType 'Basic' in the same call to switch such a wall first.

profileType.description: slantAlpha/slantBeta only have an effect once this is set to Slanted.

slantAlpha.description: Only has an effect once profileType is set to Slanted or Trapez.

slantBeta.description: Only has an effect once profileType is set to Slanted or Trapez.

topOffset.description: Only has an effect when relativeTopStory is non-zero.

relativeTopStory.description: Non-zero links the wall's top to another story instead of an explicit height - do not set together with 'height' in the same call, see the note on 'height' above.

visibility.description: Confirmed live on Archicad 29 (#852): a wall there knows only 'Home story only' and 'All relevant stories' (Wall Settings offers no Custom option), and Archicad silently drops every other combination written here although the command reports success - showAllAbove, showAllBelow, showRelAbove and showRelBelow (any value, 0 included) and showOnHome true -> false all read back unchanged. 'All relevant stories' is isAutoOnStoryVisibility true. 'Home story only' takes two calls: first isAutoOnStoryVisibility true (Archicad resets the custom fields to 0), then isAutoOnStoryVisibility false with visibility { showOnHome: true }. Archicad 30 adds a Custom option for walls; whether the other fields become writable there is untested.

isAutoOnStoryVisibility.description: When true (the default on a new wall), Archicad recomputes 'visibility' automatically from the wall's vertical extent and ignores any value set for it. Setting 'visibility' without also setting this field turns it off automatically. See the note on 'visibility' for which combinations a wall accepts.

contourPen.description: Pen of the wall's own contour/reference outline (API_WallType::contPen) - distinct from cutFillPen, which is the cut fill pattern's pen. Not inheritable/overridable like cutFillPen, it is the wall's own pen index directly, the same field regardless of structureType.

contourPen3D.description: Pen of the wall's contour in 3D views (API_WallType::contPen3D).

contourLineTypeId.description: Line type of the wall's own contour (API_WallType::contLtype) - pairs with contourPen, which only sets the pen, not the line type.

belowViewLineTypeId.description: Line type used when "OutLines Only" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup (API_WallType::belowViewLineType).

aboveViewLinePen.description: Pen used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup.

aboveViewLineTypeId.description: Line type used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup - pairs with aboveViewLinePen.

viewDepthLimitation.description: Only has an effect on a multi-story wall (relativeTopStory/topOffset making it span more than one story).

useCompositePriority.description: When true, the Composite's own priority is used at junctions instead of connectionPriority.

inheritEndSurface.description: The end surface of the wall is inherited from the adjoining wall.

alignTexture.description: Align texture mapping to the wall's edges.

polyCanChange.description: The polygonal wall's corners can be changed in case of L and T connections. Only meaningful for a Polygonal wall (geometryType).

materialsChained.description: Whether the surface materials are chained.

logHeight.description: Height of the log for log walls. 0 means a normal (non-log) wall.

commands.name: ModifyBeams
commands.description: Modifies Beam elements based on the given parameters.

width.description: Cross section width of the beam. Applied to all segments.

height.description: Cross section height of the beam. Applied to all segments.

isWidthAndHeightLinked.description: When true, Archicad keeps width and height equal and setting one changes the other - set to false first to give width/height independent values. Applied to all segments.

circleBased.description: True for a round beam cross section, false for rectangular. Ignored once profileId switches the beam to a custom profile shape. Applied to all segments.

buildingMaterialId.description: Cross section building material (round or rectangular, per circleBased). Applied to all segments.

profileId.description: Switches the cross section to this custom extruded profile (circleBased becomes false). Applied to all segments.

holes.description: Replaces all holes currently placed on the beam.

commands.name: ModifySlabs
commands.description: Modifies Slab elements based on the given parameters.

zCoordinate.description: Absolute Z of the slab's reference level. The home story is derived from it unless floorIndex is given; a Z below the lowest story stays on the lowest story with a negative level.

floorIndex.description: Optional home story index (as returned by GetStories). With zCoordinate it pins the story the Z is resolved against; alone it only changes the home story.

thickness.description: Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) slab - a Composite slab takes its thickness from the composite attribute. Send structureType 'Basic' in the same call to switch a composite slab first.

polygonOutline.description: Replaces the slab's entire polygon, including its holes - resend the holes field too to keep them, otherwise they are removed.

holes.description: Can be given on its own, without polygonOutline, to add/remove/clear holes in place (an empty array clears all holes) - the slab's current outline is reused unchanged.

commands.name: ModifyColumns
commands.description: Modifies Column elements based on the given parameters.

zCoordinate.description: Absolute Z of the column's bottom. The home story is derived from it unless floorIndex is given; a Z below the lowest story stays on the lowest story with a negative bottomOffset.

floorIndex.description: Optional home story index (as returned by GetStories). With zCoordinate it pins the story the Z is resolved against; alone it only changes the home story (combine with bottomOffset to set the offset relative to it).

height.description: Sets relativeTopStory to 0 (explicit height). Do not combine with relativeTopStory in the same call - see the note on relativeTopStory below.

isFlipped.description: Has no visible effect on a circular column (circleBased cross section) - Archicad ignores it there.

relativeTopStory.description: Non-zero links the column's top to another story instead of an explicit height - do not set together with 'height' in the same call, see the note on 'height' above.

width.description: Cross section width of the column. Applied to all segments.

depth.description: Cross section depth (height) of the column. Applied to all segments.

isWidthAndHeightLinked.description: When true, Archicad keeps width and depth equal and setting one changes the other - set to false first to give width/depth independent values. Applied to all segments.

circleBased.description: True for a round column cross section, false for rectangular. Ignored once profileId switches the column to a custom profile shape. Applied to all segments.

buildingMaterialId.description: Cross section building material (round or rectangular, per circleBased). Applied to all segments.

profileId.description: Switches the cross section to this custom extruded profile (circleBased becomes false). Applied to all segments.

commands.name: ModifyWindows
commands.description: Modifies Window elements based on the given parameters.

reveal.description: Turn the reveal on or off.

revealDepthOffset.description: Distance the frame plane is moved across the wall thickness, along the wall normal.

commands.name: ModifyDoors
commands.description: Modifies Door elements based on the given parameters.

reveal.description: Turn the reveal on or off.

revealDepthOffset.description: Distance the frame plane is moved across the wall thickness, along the wall normal.

commands.name: ModifyMorphs
commands.description: Modifies Morph elements based on the given parameters.

rotationDegreesZ.description: Turns the Morph about the vertical axis through its origin, counterclockwise seen from above, in degrees. Added to the current rotation.

body.description: When given, discards the Morph's ENTIRE existing geometry and rebuilds it from this (mirrors CreateProfiles' replaceSkins) - not a partial edit.

xAxis.description: Replaces the rotation part of the placement transform outright. Give all three of xAxis/yAxis/zAxis together. If rotationDegreesZ is also given in the same call, it is applied first and this then overwrites its result.

commands.name: ModifyRoofs
commands.description: Modifies multi-plane Roof elements based on the given parameters.

thickness.description: Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) roof - a Composite roof takes its thickness from the composite attribute. Send structureType 'Basic' in the same call to switch a composite roof first.

commands.name: ModifyMeshes
commands.description: Modifies the attributes of Mesh elements based on the given parameters.

commands.name: ModifyObjects
commands.description: Modifies Object elements based on the given parameters.

objectsWithDetails.description: Array of elements to modify, with the fields to change. Only provided fields are changed; omitted fields are left as-is.

fixPoint.description: 0-based index of the hotspot to keep fixed (raw API_ObjectType.fixPoint value, not 1-based).

offset.description: Offset of the symbol's origin from the insertion point. Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify (Get always reports the library part's own default hotspot offset regardless of what is sent) - same class of read-only-in-practice field as Morph's bodyType/edgeType/level.

useFixedAngle.description: Use a fixed rotation angle. Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify.

commands.name: ModifyLamps
commands.description: Modifies Lamp elements based on the given parameters.

lampsWithDetails.description: Array of elements to modify, with the fields to change. Only provided fields are changed; omitted fields are left as-is.

fixPoint.description: 0-based index of the hotspot to keep fixed (raw API_ObjectType.fixPoint value, not 1-based).

offset.description: Offset of the symbol's origin from the insertion point. Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify (Get always reports the library part's own default hotspot offset regardless of what is sent) - same class of read-only-in-practice field as Morph's bodyType/edgeType/level.

useFixedAngle.description: Use a fixed rotation angle. Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify.

lightColor.description: Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify (Get always reports the library part's own default light color). lightIsOn (the on/off state, as opposed to the color) does not have this problem.

commands.name: ModifyTexts
commands.description: Modifies standalone Text elements based on the given parameters.

textsWithDetails.description: Array of Text elements to modify, with the fields to change. Only provided fields are changed; omitted fields are left as-is. A change of the text, the runs, or a run-level style field (pen, font, faces, height, effects) rebuilds the content as one paragraph, which makes the element auto-width (word wrap off), as SetDetailsOfElements does, and on a multi-run text applies that style to every run; the other style fields leave the content as it is.

coordinate.description: The new placement position. As in CreateTexts, the z value selects the floor when floorIndex is omitted.

floorIndex.description: Optional. Moves the text to this floor; when omitted and a coordinate is given, the floor is derived from its z value.

text.description: The new text content. Newlines create multiple lines; Windows-style CRLF (and bare CR) line endings are normalized to LF.

commands.name: ModifyLabels
commands.description: Modifies Label elements based on the given parameters.

labelsWithDetails.description: Array of Label elements to modify, with the fields to change. Only provided fields are changed; omitted fields are left as-is. The label's class (Text/Symbol) cannot be changed after creation. A change of the text, the runs, or a run-level style field (pen, font, faces, height, effects) rebuilds the content as one paragraph, which makes the label's text auto-width (word wrap off), as SetDetailsOfElements does, and on a multi-run label applies that style to every run; the other style fields leave the content as it is.

text.description: The new text content. Newlines create multiple lines; Windows-style CRLF (and bare CR) line endings are normalized to LF.

commands.name: MeasureTexts
commands.description: Measures texts before placing them: the length of every line for a given font, style and height, on paper in millimetres or in the model at the current drawing scale, and the font's capital size factor. Creates nothing.

texts.description: The texts to measure, each with the font, style and height it would be placed with. Nothing is created.

text.description: The text to measure. Newlines separate lines, each measured on its own; Windows-style CRLF (and bare CR) line endings are treated as LF.

fontIndex.description: The index of the font, as GetDetailsOfElements reports it in fontIndex.

fontName.description: Name of the font, as the Font attributes carry it and GetDetailsOfElements reports it in fontName, e.g. 'Arial'. Resolved to the font's index (exact match first, then case-insensitive); the text fails when no loaded font has the name. Takes precedence over fontIndex if both are given. One of fontName and fontIndex is required.

height.description: The character height in millimetres, as a Text's height.

slant.description: The slant angle of the characters in radians; pi/2 (the default) is upright text.

inModelUnits.description: When true, Archicad applies the drawing scale correction and the lengths are model distances at the current drawing scale; when false (the default), they are lengths on paper in millimetres.

measurements.description: One item per input text, in the same order. The measurement takes no width factor or character spacing into account.

length.description: The length of the longest line.

longestLineIndex.description: The zero-based index of the longest line (the first of them on a tie).

lineLengths.description: The length of every line, in order. An empty line is 0.

capitalSizeFactor.description: The ratio of the font's capital size to its typographic size. Absent when Archicad does not return it for the font.

commands.name: RegularizePolygons
commands.description: Regularizes polygons with Archicad's own polygon regularization, before they are used to create slabs, zones or fills: removes duplicate points, fixes the orientation, resolves self-intersections and touching holes. Each input polygon gives 0, 1 or more valid polygons in the format of CreateSlabs, optionally with the input vertex and edge each result vertex and edge came from. Changes nothing in the project.

withAncestry.description: Also return for every vertex and edge of the results which input vertex or edge it came from. Optional, false by default.

results.description: One item per input polygon, in the order of the request.

polygons.description: The valid polygons Archicad made of the input: none, one or more.

polygonCoordinates.description: The 2D coordinates of the outline, without a closing coordinate.

ancestry.description: Only with withAncestry. Read from the vertexAncestry and edgeAncestry of Archicad's API_RegularizedPoly; -1 marks a vertex or edge that Archicad created (for example at a self-intersection).

contours.description: One item per contour of this result: the outline first, then the holes in order.

vertices.description: For each vertex of the contour, the input vertex it came from.

items.description: An input vertex or edge: the contour (0 is the outline, k the hole at index k-1 of the request) and the vertex or edge in it (edge i runs from vertex i to the next one). Both are -1 when Archicad created it.

edges.description: For each edge of the contour (edge i runs from vertex i to the next one), the input edge it came from.

items.description: An input vertex or edge: the contour (0 is the outline, k the hole at index k-1 of the request) and the vertex or edge in it (edge i runs from vertex i to the next one). Both are -1 when Archicad created it.

The result is in the format of CreatePolylines and may be empty, optionally with the input point and segment each result point and segment came from. Changes nothing in the project.

polylines.description: The polylines to regularize, in the format of CreatePolylines.

withAncestry.description: Also return for every point and segment of the results which input point or segment it came from. Optional, false by default.

results.description: One item per input polyline, in the order of the request.

coordinates.description: The 2D coordinates of the regularized polyline. Empty when nothing valid is left of it.

arcs.description: The arcs of the regularized polyline.

ancestry.description: Only with withAncestry. Read from the vertexAncestry and edgeAncestry of Archicad's API_RegularizedPoly; -1 marks a vertex or edge that Archicad created (for example at a self-intersection).

vertices.description: For each point of the result, the index of the input point it came from.

items.description: An input point or segment by its index (segment i runs from point i to point i+1); -1 when Archicad created it.

edges.description: For each segment of the result (segment i runs from point i to point i+1), the index of the input segment it came from.

items.description: An input point or segment by its index (segment i runs from point i to point i+1); -1 when Archicad created it.

commands.name: ApplyFavoritesToElements
commands.description: Apply the given favorites to existing elements. Only settings-type parameters are changed - geometry (position, floor, and dimensions such as a Wall's height) is left untouched, so applying a Favorite never moves or resizes the target element. For the hierarchical types (Stair, Railing, Curtain Wall) the settings of the sub-elements are not applied, because they are inseparable from the Favorite's own geometry. By default settings, classifications, categories and properties are all applied; each can be opted out of individually. keepFields lists fields of the target (its ID, layer, an opening's width, height and sill height, a Wall's reference line location, height and top link) that are copied back after the Favorite has been applied, so that e.g. only the library part or the wall type changes.

items.description: The identifier of the element and the name of the Favorite to apply to it.

applySettings.description: Whether to apply the Favorite's settings-type parameters (structure, materials, pens, etc. - never geometry). For the hierarchical types (Stair, Railing, Curtain Wall) the settings of the sub-elements are not applied, because they are inseparable from the Favorite's own geometry. Default is true.

applyClassifications.description: Whether to apply the Favorite's classifications. Default is true.

applyCategories.description: Whether to apply the Favorite's element categories (e.g. IFC categories). Default is true.

applyProperties.description: Whether to apply the Favorite's property values. Default is true.

keepFields.description: Fields of the target element to keep: after the Favorite has been applied, they are copied back from the target as it was before, so only the Favorite's other settings (e.g. its library part or wall type) take effect. 'id' and 'layerIndex' apply to every element type; 'width', 'height' and 'sillHeight' to a Window or Door ('width' and 'height' also to a Skylight); 'height', 'topOffset' and 'relativeTopStory' to a Wall or Column; 'referenceLineLocation' to a Wall. A field the target's type does not have is ignored. To keep a Wall's or Column's top exactly as it was, keep 'height', 'relativeTopStory' and 'topOffset' together - a kept 'height' alone is recomputed by Archicad while the Favorite's relativeTopStory links the top to a story. Default: nothing is kept.

fillBackgroundPen.description: The index of the background pen [0..255]. 0 means transparent background.

centerLinePen.description: The index of the center line pen [1..255].

fillId.description: Identifier of the fill pattern attribute.

centerLineTypeId.description: Identifier of the center line type attribute.

materialId.description: Identifier of the surface (material) attribute applied to the 3D model of the elements of the system.

insulationMaterialId.description: Identifier of the surface (material) attribute applied to the insulation of the elements of the system.

overwriteExisting.description: Overwrite the MEP System if exists with the same name, or if index is given with the same index. The default is false.

commands.name: CreatePenTables
commands.description: Creates or overwrites Pen Table attributes based on the given parameters.

penTableDataArray.description: Array of data to create new Pen Tables.

items.description: Data to create a Pen Table.

attributeId.description: Indentifier of the existing Pen Table to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

index.description: Index of the existing Pen Table to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

name.description: Name. If overwriteExisting is true, then the existing Pen Table with the given name will be overwritten.

isActiveForModel.description: Make this the active Pen Table for the model window. Defaults to false for a new Pen Table, or to the current value when overwriting an existing one.

isActiveForLayout.description: Make this the active Pen Table for layouts. Defaults to false for a new Pen Table, or to the current value when overwriting an existing one.

sourceAttributeId.description: Identifier of the Pen Table whose 255 pens are used as the starting point, before the pens listed in the pens array are applied on top. Defaults to the Pen Table being overwritten itself (so unlisted pens keep their current color/width/description), or an arbitrary existing Pen Table in the project when creating a brand new one (or a plain black, 0.1 mm pen for all 255 if the project has no Pen Table at all yet).

pens.description: The pens to set in the Pen Table, on top of the 255 pens copied from sourceAttributeId (or the current Pen Table, or an arbitrary existing one - see sourceAttributeId). Only list the pens you actually want to change.

overwriteExisting.description: Overwrite the Pen Table if exists with the same name, or if index is given with the same index. The default is false.

commands.name: CreateProfiles
commands.description: Creates or overwrites Profile attributes as a copy of an existing Profile's geometry, based on the given parameters.

profileDataArray.description: Array of data to create new Profiles.

items.description: Data to create or modify a Profile. Its geometry (the cross-section shape) comes from sourceAttributeId (an existing Profile's geometry, copied), from newSkins (AC27+ only, caller-supplied polygon geometry), or both combined. When creating a brand-new Profile (overwriteExisting false, or true but no existing match), at least one of the two must be given. When overwriteExisting targets an existing Profile, both are optional - the existing Profile's own current geometry is preserved by default (e.g. to change only wallType, or to add newSkins on top of the unchanged existing shape). skinOverrides and newSkins' edgeOverrides target skins/edges by the identifiers/indices GetProfiles reports.

attributeId.description: Indentifier of the existing Profile to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

index.description: Index of the existing Profile to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

name.description: Name. If overwriteExisting is true, then the existing Profile with the given name will be overwritten.

sourceAttributeId.description: Identifier of an existing Profile whose geometry (cross-section shape) will be copied as the starting point. Optional if newSkins is given: omit it to build the Profile's geometry entirely from newSkins instead of copying anything (AC27+ only).

wallType.description: Profile available for walls. Defaults to the source Profile's value.

beamType.description: Profile available for beams. Defaults to the source Profile's value.

coluType.description: Profile available for columns. Defaults to the source Profile's value.

handrailType.description: Profile available for handrails. Defaults to the source Profile's value.

otherGDLObjectType.description: Profile available for other GDL based objects. Defaults to the source Profile's value.

skinOverrides.description: Modifications to apply to specific skins of the copied geometry, e.g. to change a skin's building material without rebuilding the profile's shape. Each skinId comes from a prior GetProfiles call's skins[].skinId on the source Profile (or, when overwriteExisting is true, on the Profile being overwritten).

skinId.description: Identifies which skin to modify, from GetProfiles' skins[].skinId.

edgeOverrides.description: Modifications to specific edges of this skin, targeted by their position (0-based) in GetProfiles' skins[].edges.

newSkins.description: AC27+ only. Adds brand-new skins built from caller-supplied polygon geometry, instead of (or in addition to) whatever was copied from sourceAttributeId. Combine with sourceAttributeId to add skins to a copied Profile, or omit sourceAttributeId to build a Profile's geometry entirely from newSkins.

replaceSkins.description: AC27+ only. When overwriteExisting targets an existing Profile, discard every one of its existing skins (and any sourceAttributeId geometry given alongside it) before applying newSkins, instead of adding newSkins on top of the preserved existing geometry. Use this to fully replace a Profile's cross-section with a caller-authored shape while keeping its guid and scalar fields (wallType etc.) - e.g. to sync a Profile's geometry from another project, where sourceAttributeId can't be used because it only resolves within the same file. Also discards any existing profileModifiers, since those are tied to the specific geometry being replaced. Ignored when creating a brand-new Profile (there is nothing to discard yet).

overwriteExisting.description: Overwrite the Profile if exists with the same name, or if index is given with the same index. The default is false.

commands.name: CreateBuildingMaterials
commands.description: Creates or overwrites Building Material attributes based on the given parameters.

buildingMaterialDataArray.description: Array of data to create new Building Materials.

items.description: Data to create a Building Material.

attributeId.description: Indentifier of the existing Building Material to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

index.description: Index of the existing Building Material to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

name.description: Name. If overwriteExisting is true, then the existing Building Material with the given name will be overwritten.

id.description: Identifier.

collisionDetection.description: Whether the Building Material participates in collision detection.

cutFillOrientation.description: ProjectOrigin, ElementOrigin, or FitToSkin. Orientation of the cut fill.

overwriteExisting.description: Overwrite the Building Material if exists with the same name, or if index is given with the same index. The default is false.

commands.name: CreateComposites
commands.description: Creates or overwrites Composite attributes based on the given parameters.

compositeDataArray.description: Array of data to create Composites.

items.description: Data to create a Composite.

attributeId.description: Indentifier of the existing Composite to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

index.description: Index of the existing Composite to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

name.description: Name. If overwriteExisting is true, then the existing Composite with the given name will be overwritten.

useWith.description: Array of types the composite can used with.

items.description: Element type (Wall, Slab, Roof, or Shell)
Data to represent a skin.

separators.description: Array of skin separator data. The number of items must be the number of skins plus one.

items.description: Data to represent a skin separator.

overwriteExisting.description: Overwrite the Composite if exists with the same name, or if index is given with the same index. The default is false.

commands.name: CreateSurfaces
commands.description: Creates or overwrites Surface attributes based on the given parameters.

surfaceDataArray.description: Array of data to create new surfaces.

items.description: Data to create a surface.

attributeId.description: Indentifier of the existing Surface to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

index.description: Index of the existing surface to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

name.description: Name. If overwriteExisting is true, then the existing surface with the given name will be overwritten.

overwriteExisting.description: Overwrite the Surface if exists with the same name, or if index is given with the same index. The default is false.

commands.name: GetBuildingMaterialPhysicalProperties
commands.description: Retrieves the physical properties of the given Building Materials.

commands.name: GetLayerCombinations
commands.description: Returns the details of layer combination attributes.

commands.name: GetCurrentLayerCombination
commands.description: Returns the layer combination in effect in the current window. No layer combination is returned when the current state of the layers matches none.

layerCombinationId.description: The layer combination in effect in the current window. Missing when the current state of the layers matches no layer combination.

name.description: The name of the layer combination. Missing together with layerCombinationId.

commands.name: GetLines
commands.description: Returns the details of the given Line attributes.

fields.description: Names of the fields to return for each Line. If omitted, every field is returned. Requesting only the fields you need avoids fetching dashItems/lineItems, which can be large.

lines.description: A list of lines or errors.

commands.name: GetFills
commands.description: Returns the details of the given Fill attributes.

fields.description: Names of the fields to return for each Fill. If omitted, every field is returned. Requesting only the fields you need avoids fetching lineItems/symbolLines/symbolArcs/symbolHotspots, which can be large.

fills.description: A list of fills or errors.

commands.name: GetZoneCategories
commands.description: Returns the details of the given Zone Category attributes.

fields.description: Names of the fields to return for each Zone Category. If omitted, every field is returned.

zoneCategories.description: A list of zone categories or errors.

commands.name: GetMEPSystems
commands.description: Returns the details of the given MEP System attributes (domain, pens, fill, center line type, surface and insulation surface).

fields.description: Names of the fields to return for each MEP System. If omitted, every field is returned.

mepSystems.description: A list of MEP systems or errors.

commands.name: GetPenTables
commands.description: Returns the details of the given Pen Table attributes.

fields.description: Names of the fields to return for each Pen Table. If omitted, every field is returned. Requesting only the fields you need avoids fetching the 255-element pens array.

penTables.description: A list of pen tables or errors.

commands.name: GetCurrentPenTable
commands.description: Returns the current Pen Table (its index, attribute identifier and name) and its number of pens. Pass the returned attributeId to GetPenTables to read the pens.

index.description: The attribute index of the current Pen Table, as returned by Archicad.

isPenTableAttribute.description: True if the index refers to an existing Pen Table attribute. When false, attributeId and name are omitted; the pens in effect can not be read with GetPenTables.

name.description: The name of the current Pen Table attribute.

penCount.description: The number of pens in the current Pen Table. Omitted when it can not be read.

commands.name: GetProfiles
commands.description: Returns the details of the given Profile attributes.

fields.description: Names of the fields to return for each Profile. If omitted, every field is returned. Note the raw cross-section vector geometry itself is not exposed; width/height/minimumWidth/minimumHeight/widthStretchable/heightStretchable/hasCoreSkin/profileModifiers are derived measurements matching what the Profile Editor shows, computed from the profile's internal stretch/parameter data.

profiles.description: A list of profiles or errors.

commands.name: GetComposites
commands.description: Returns the details of the given Composite attributes.

fields.description: Names of the fields to return for each Composite. If omitted, every field is returned.

composites.description: A list of composites or errors.

commands.name: GetSurfaces
commands.description: Returns the details of the given Surface attributes.

fields.description: Names of the fields to return for each Surface. If omitted, every field is returned.

surfaces.description: A list of surfaces or errors.

commands.name: GetLayers
commands.description: Returns the details of the given Layer attributes.

fields.description: Names of the fields to return for each Layer. If omitted, every field is returned.

layers.description: A list of layers or errors.

commands.name: GetBuildingMaterials
commands.description: Returns the details of the given Building Material attributes.

fields.description: Names of the fields to return for each Building Material. If omitted, every field is returned.

buildingMaterials.description: A list of building materials or errors.

commands.name: GetFontsByName
commands.description: Finds loaded fonts by name through Archicad's font search and returns their index (as Text and Label fields reference fonts in fontIndex) and name, or an error for a name no loaded font has.

fontNames.description: Names of the fonts to find, as the Text tool's font list shows them and GetDetailsOfElements reports them in fontName, e.g. 'Arial'.

fonts.description: One item per name, in the order given: the font found, or an error when no loaded font has the name.

fontIndex.description: Index of the font (from 1), as Text and Label fields reference it in fontIndex.

fontName.description: Name of the font as Archicad carries it.

commands.name: GetGraphicOverrideRules
commands.description: Gets all graphic override rules of the project, with their rule group, criterion and style. Available from Archicad 27.

graphicOverrideRules.description: The graphic override rules of the project.

commands.name: GetGraphicOverrideRulesByName
commands.description: Gets graphic override rules by name, with their rule group, criterion and style. The rule group narrows the search; without it the rule is searched in every rule group. Available from Archicad 27.

graphicOverrideRules.description: The graphic override rules to get, by name.

name.description: The name of the rule. Rule names are unique within the project.

ruleGroupName.description: The name of the rule group to search the rule in. Left out: every rule group is searched.

graphicOverrideRules.description: The rules, or errors, in the order of the input.

commands.name: CreateGraphicOverrideRules
commands.description: Creates graphic override rules. The criterion is given as Archicad's criterion XML or as structured conditions. The rule group is created when no rule group has the given name. Available from Archicad 27.

graphicOverrideRules.description: The graphic override rules to create.

name.description: The name of the rule, unique within the project.

ruleGroupName.description: The name of the rule group to put the rule in. Created when it does not exist.

criterionXML.description: The criterion of the rule, in the XML format Archicad saves override rules in. Take it from GetGraphicOverrideRules and change its values: Archicad drops XML written from scratch without an error, and the rule then applies to all elements. Left out together with 'criterion': Archicad's default criterion for new rules.

criterion.description: The criterion of the rule as structured conditions, turned into Archicad's criterion XML. Use it instead of criterionXML, not with it.

graphicOverrideRuleIds.description: The identifiers of the created rules, or errors, in the order of the input.

commands.name: ModifyGraphicOverrideRules
commands.description: Modifies the name, criterion or style of graphic override rules. The criterion is given as Archicad's criterion XML or as structured conditions. A given style replaces the whole style of the rule. Available from Archicad 27.

graphicOverrideRules.description: The graphic override rules to modify.

name.description: The new name of the rule.

criterionXML.description: The new criterion of the rule, in the XML format Archicad saves override rules in. Take it from GetGraphicOverrideRules and change its values: Archicad drops XML written from scratch without an error, and the rule then applies to all elements.

criterion.description: The new criterion of the rule as structured conditions, turned into Archicad's criterion XML. Use it instead of criterionXML, not with it.

commands.name: DeleteGraphicOverrideRules
commands.description: Deletes graphic override rules. They are also removed from the combinations that contain them. Available from Archicad 27.

graphicOverrideRuleIds.description: The graphic override rules to delete.

commands.name: GetGraphicOverrideCombinations
commands.description: Gets all graphic override combinations of the project with the rules they contain. Available from Archicad 27.

graphicOverrideCombinations.description: The graphic override combinations of the project.

graphicOverrideRuleIds.description: The rules of the combination, in priority order.

commands.name: CreateGraphicOverrideCombinations
commands.description: Creates graphic override combinations from existing rules. Available from Archicad 27.

graphicOverrideCombinations.description: The graphic override combinations to create.

name.description: The name of the combination, unique within the project.

graphicOverrideRuleIds.description: The rules of the combination, in priority order.

graphicOverrideCombinationIds.description: The identifiers of the created combinations, or errors, in the order of the input.

commands.name: DeleteGraphicOverrideCombinations
commands.description: Deletes graphic override combinations. Their rules are kept. Available from Archicad 27.

graphicOverrideCombinationIds.description: The graphic override combinations to delete. Their rules are kept.

commands.name: GetGraphicOverrideRuleGroups
commands.description: Gets all graphic override rule groups of the project with the rules they contain, empty groups included. Available from Archicad 27.

graphicOverrideRuleGroups.description: The graphic override rule groups of the project, empty ones included.

commands.name: RenameGraphicOverrideRuleGroups
commands.description: Renames graphic override rule groups, found by name. Their rules are kept. Available from Archicad 27.

ruleGroups.description: The rule groups to rename. Their rules and the combinations that contain them are kept.

name.description: The current name of the rule group.

newName.description: The new name of the rule group. It must not be empty or used by another rule group.

commands.name: DeleteGraphicOverrideRuleGroups
commands.description: Deletes graphic override rule groups, found by name. A group that still contains rules is kept unless its rules are moved to another group or deleted with it. Available from Archicad 27.

ruleGroupNames.description: The names of the rule groups to delete.

moveRulesToGroup.description: The name of the rule group the rules of the deleted groups are moved to, so they are kept. Created when no rule group has this name.

deleteRules.description: Delete the rules of the deleted groups too. Without this or moveRulesToGroup, a group that still contains rules is not deleted.

commands.name: MoveGraphicOverrideRules
commands.description: Moves graphic override rules to another rule group, or to another place in their own group. Available from Archicad 27.

graphicOverrideRules.description: The rules to move, processed in this order.

ruleGroupName.description: The rule group the rule is moved to; it can be the rule's own group to change its place there. Created when no rule group has this name.

beforeGraphicOverrideRuleId.description: The rule of the target group the moved rule is put in front of. Left out: the rule becomes the last of the group.

commands.name: IFCFileOperation
commands.description: Executes an IFC file operation: opens or merges an IFC file, or saves the project as an IFC file. A save can name the export translator to use.

method.description: The file operation method to use.

ifcFilePath.description: The target IFC file to use.

fileType.description: The type of the IFC file. The default is 'ifc'.

translatorName.description: Only for the save method: the name of the IFC export translator to save with, as GetIFCExportTranslators lists them. Without it the save runs with the translator Archicad would offer in its own Save dialog. Needs a fileType of ifc or ifczip (ifc or ifcxml on Archicad 25 and 26).

elementsToExport.description: Only for the save method, and only together with translatorName. The default is VisibleElementsOnAllStories.

commands.name: GetIFCExportTranslators
commands.description: Lists the IFC export translators of the project, the preview translator first. Pass one of the names to IFCFileOperation as translatorName.

translators.description: The IFC export translators of the project, the preview translator first.

commands.name: GetElementsByIFCIds
commands.description: Retrieves the elements by the given IFC identifiers.

ifcIds.description: A list of IFC identifiers to get the corresponding elements for.

commands.name: GetIFCIdsOfElements
commands.description: Retrieves the IFC identifiers of the given elements.

commands.name: GetIFCTypeOfElements
commands.description: Retrieves the IFC types of the given elements.

commands.name: GetIFCPropertiesOfElements
commands.description: Retrieves the IFC properties of the given elements.

commands.name: GetIFCAttributesOfElements
commands.description: Retrieves the IFC attributes (Name, Description, ObjectType, Tag, PredefinedType, LongName, ...) of the given elements, subelements included: the name, the IFC value type and the value of each attribute. On Archicad 25, 26 and 27 storedOnly returns only the attributes stored on the elements.

storedOnly.description: Return only the attributes stored on the elements, not the ones Archicad would generate on IFC export. Used only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27. Default: false.

commands.name: SetIFCAttributesOfElements
commands.description: Sets the values of IFC attributes (Name, Description, ObjectType, Tag, ...) of elements. The attribute must be one GetIFCAttributesOfElements returns for the element; its IFC value type is kept. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 for now.

elementIFCAttributeValues.description: The IFC attribute values to set.

name.description: The name of the IFC attribute, for example Name, Description, ObjectType or Tag. It must be one of the attributes GetIFCAttributesOfElements returns for the element.

value.description: The new value of the IFC attribute.

commands.name: SetIFCPropertiesOfElements
commands.description: Sets local IFC properties on elements by creating or modifying single value (IfcPropertySingleValue) properties in the given property sets. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 for now.

elementIFCPropertyValues.description: The IFC property values to set. Only single value (IfcPropertySingleValue) properties are supported.

propertySetName.description: The name of the property set, for example Pset_DoorCommon. Custom property set names are also accepted.

propertyName.description: The name of the property, for example FireRating.

type.description: The IFC type of the value, for example IfcLabel, IfcText, IfcIdentifier, IfcBoolean, IfcLogical, IfcInteger, IfcReal or a measure type like IfcThermalTransmittanceMeasure. A type Archicad does not know is rejected.

value.description: The new value of the property. Provide a boolean for IfcBoolean and IfcLogical (IfcLogical also accepts the string Unknown), a number for the numeric types and a string for every other type.

commands.name: RemoveIFCPropertiesOfElements
commands.description: Removes local IFC properties, given by property set and property name, from elements. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 for now.

elementIFCProperties.description: The local IFC properties to remove.

propertySetName.description: The name of the property set, for example Pset_DoorCommon.

propertyName.description: The name of the property, for example FireRating.

commands.name: GetLibraries
commands.description: Gets the list of loaded libraries.

commands.name: ReloadLibraries
commands.description: Executes the reload libraries command.

commands.name: AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary
commands.description: Adds the given files into the embedded library. With the overwriteExisting flag an embedded library item already existing on an outputPath is replaced (Archicad 27 or newer).

overwriteExisting.description: Optional. When true, an embedded library item already existing on an outputPath is deleted first, so the newly added file replaces the loaded library part. By default false: the existing loaded part stays in use. Requires Archicad 27 or newer.

commands.name: DeleteEmbeddedLibraryItems
commands.description: Deletes the given items from the embedded library. The path of an item is the same relative path that AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary takes as outputPath. Available from Archicad 27.

embeddedLibraryItems.description: A list of embedded library items to delete.

path.description: The relative path of the library item inside the embedded library, the same path AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary takes as outputPath.

commands.name: CreateFolderInEmbeddedLibrary
commands.description: Creates a folder, with any missing parent folders, inside the embedded library. The folderPath is relative to the embedded library, like the outputPath of AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary.

folderPath.description: The path of the folder relative to the embedded library, for example 'Office/Doors'. Missing parent folders are created too; folders that already exist are kept.

commands.name: CopyFilesIntoEmbeddedLibrary
commands.description: Copies the given files, keeping their names, into a folder of the embedded library with one library operation. The target folder is created when it is missing. With overwriteIfExists an item of the same name in that folder is replaced.

files.description: The files to copy. Each keeps its file name inside the target folder.

path.description: The absolute path of the file to copy.

targetFolder.description: Optional. The folder relative to the embedded library to copy the files into, for example 'Office/Doors'. Missing folders are created. By default the root of the embedded library.

overwriteIfExists.description: Optional. When true, an item with the same name in the target folder is replaced. By default false.

commands.name: SetLibraries
commands.description: Makes the given folders the project's local libraries; built-in, embedded, server and web libraries are kept. Set the libraries before opening a file that needs them and the missing-library dialog does not appear.

libraries.description: Local library folders or container files, by absolute path.

commands.name: AddLibraries
commands.description: Adds the given folders to the project's local libraries, skipping any already loaded.

libraries.description: Local library folders or container files, by absolute path.

commands.name: GetAvailableLibraryParts
commands.description: Lists library parts currently available to the project. Filter by typeId (e.g. 'Door', 'Window', 'Object', 'Lamp').

filterByTypeId.description: Optional. Filter by libpart type (matches the value returned by LibPartTypeIdToString).

skippedCount.description: Library parts that ACAPI_LibraryPart_Get failed to read. Non-zero means the inventory is partial.

skippedSample.description: First five failed indices with their ACAPI error code, for diagnostic.

commands.name: SetLibraryPartScripts
commands.description: Sets the master, parameter, 2D, 3D and properties scripts of loaded library parts. Only the given scripts are changed; an empty script makes the section empty. A library part that is not editable (e.g. a part of a library package or a read-only library) is refused and left unchanged. Available from Archicad 28.

libraryParts.description: The library parts to modify and the scripts to set in each.

name.description: The name of the loaded library part file with its extension, as returned in the fileName field of GetAvailableLibraryParts (e.g. 'My Door.gsm').

scripts.description: The scripts to set. Only the scripts given here are changed, the others are kept. An empty string makes that script section empty, it does not delete it.

commands.name: TeamworkSend
commands.description: Performs a send operation on the currently opened Teamwork project.

commands.name: TeamworkReceive
commands.description: Performs a receive operation on the currently opened Teamwork project.

commands.name: ReserveElements
commands.description: Reserves elements in Teamwork mode.

commands.name: ReleaseElements
commands.description: Releases elements in Teamwork mode.

commands.name: GetReservationStatusOfElements
commands.description: Returns the Teamwork reservation status of elements without reserving them: whether each element is free, reserved by the current user or reserved by another user, with the reserving user and the element's owner.

reservationStatuses.description: One item per input element, in the same order.

status.description: Free: nobody has reserved the element. Editable: the current user has reserved it. Locked: another user has reserved it (see reservedBy).

reservedBy.description: The user who has reserved the element. Left out when the element is free.

owner.description: The user who owns the element in Teamwork, usually the one who created it. Left out when the element has no owner.

commands.name: GrantElements
commands.description: Hands over the reservation of elements to another Teamwork user, given by user id, without a dialog. Available from Archicad 27.

userId.description: The Teamwork user id of the user to hand the elements over to, as GetTeamworkProjectInfo, GetReservationStatusOfElements and the conflicts of ReserveElements report users.

commands.name: ReserveLockableObjectSet
commands.description: Reserves a non-element lockable object set (attributes, favorites, project info, project preferences, etc.) in Teamwork mode. The object set is given by its Archicad API name, e.g. 'Composites', 'LayerSettingsDialog' or 'ProjectInfo'.

objectSetName.description: The name of the lockable object set, as the Archicad API documents it: BuildingMaterials, Cities, Composites, Favorites, FillTypes, LayerSettingsDialog (layers and layer combinations), LineTypes, MarkupStyles, MEPSystems, ModelViewOptions, OperationProfiles, PenTables, Profiles, ProjectInfo, GeoLocation (project location), PreferencesDialog (project preferences and dimension standards), GraphicOverrides (renovation override styles), Surfaces or ZoneCategories. Other names the Archicad API accepts work too.

conflicts.description: The users whose reservation prevented reserving the object set.

commands.name: ReleaseLockableObjectSet
commands.description: Releases a non-element lockable object set reserved with ReserveLockableObjectSet in Teamwork mode.

objectSetName.description: The name of the lockable object set, as the Archicad API documents it: BuildingMaterials, Cities, Composites, Favorites, FillTypes, LayerSettingsDialog (layers and layer combinations), LineTypes, MarkupStyles, MEPSystems, ModelViewOptions, OperationProfiles, PenTables, Profiles, ProjectInfo, GeoLocation (project location), PreferencesDialog (project preferences and dimension standards), GraphicOverrides (renovation override styles), Surfaces or ZoneCategories. Other names the Archicad API accepts work too.

commands.name: GetLockableObjectSetStatus
commands.description: Returns the Teamwork reservation status of a non-element lockable object set and the users who hold it.

objectSetName.description: The name of the lockable object set, as the Archicad API documents it: BuildingMaterials, Cities, Composites, Favorites, FillTypes, LayerSettingsDialog (layers and layer combinations), LineTypes, MarkupStyles, MEPSystems, ModelViewOptions, OperationProfiles, PenTables, Profiles, ProjectInfo, GeoLocation (project location), PreferencesDialog (project preferences and dimension standards), GraphicOverrides (renovation override styles), Surfaces or ZoneCategories. Other names the Archicad API accepts work too.

status.description: Free: nobody has reserved it. Editable: the current user has reserved it. Locked: another user has reserved it (see conflicts). NotAvailable: the Teamwork server is offline or not available. NotExist: there is no Teamwork connection, for example the project is not a Teamwork project. An unknown object set name is reported as an error, not as a status.

conflicts.description: The users who hold a reservation on the object set.

commands.name: ReserveHotlinkCacheManagement
commands.description: Reserves the Hotlink and XRef management in Teamwork mode, which is needed before changing hotlink nodes.

conflicts.description: The user whose reservation prevented reserving the Hotlink and XRef management.

commands.name: ReleaseHotlinkCacheManagement
commands.description: Releases the Hotlink and XRef management in Teamwork mode.

commands.name: GetTeamworkStatus
commands.description: Returns whether the opened project is a Teamwork project and is online, the members of the shared project and who has reserved the Hotlink and XRef management. Works in a solo project too, then isShared and isOnline are false.

isShared.description: Whether the opened project is a Teamwork (BIMcloud) project.

isOnline.description: Whether there is a live connection to the Teamwork server. Always false for a project that is not shared.

users.description: The members of the shared project. Only present when the project is shared.

userName.description: The login name of the user.

isConnected.description: Whether the user has joined the project.

hotlinkCacheManagementOwner.description: The user who has reserved the Hotlink and XRef management. Only present when somebody has reserved it.

commands.name: PublishPublisherSet
commands.description: Performs a publish operation on the currently opened project. Only the given publisher set will be published.

publisherSetName.description: The name of the publisher set.

outputPath.description: Full local or LAN path for publishing. Optional, by default the path set in the settings of the publisher set will be used.

selectedNavigatorItemIds.description: Optional publisher-tree navigator items to publish instead of the whole publisher set.

commands.name: UpdateDrawings
commands.description: Performs a drawing update on the given elements.

commands.name: GetDrawingContentBoxes
commands.description: Returns the full content box of the given Drawing elements, independent of their frames, as ACAPI_Drawing_GetFullDrawingContentBox reports it. Available from Archicad 27.

contentBoxes.description: One item per input element, in the same order: the full content box of the Drawing, or an error.

contentBox.description: The full boundary box of the Drawing's content, independent of its frame, as returned by Archicad.

commands.name: GetDatabaseIdFromNavigatorItemId
commands.description: Gets the ID of the database associated with the supplied navigator item id

commands.name: GetDatabases
commands.description: Lists every database of the given types (sections, elevations, interior elevations, details, worksheets, 3D documents, layouts, master layouts) with its database ID, name and reference ID, without walking the navigator trees.

types.description: The types of the databases to list. Optional, by default the databases of every type are listed.

name.description: The name of the database. Missing when the database info cannot be read.

referenceId.description: The reference id of the database. Missing when the database info cannot be read.

commands.name: CreateDetails
commands.description: Creates independent Detail databases.

commands.name: CreateWorksheets
commands.description: Creates independent Worksheet databases.

commands.name: CreateLayout
commands.description: Creates Layouts and their backing master layouts. Archicad inserts a new layout at the first place of its subset, renumbering the sheets after it; previousNavigatorItemId or position 'last' places it after an existing sheet or at the end instead.

previousNavigatorItemId.description: The sibling after which the new layout is placed, as in MoveNavigatorItem. It must be a child of parentNavigatorItemId (or of the Layout Book root when that is omitted). Cannot be combined with position.

position.description: Where to place the new layout under its parent. Archicad inserts new layouts at the first place, which renumbers the sheets after them; "last" appends it after the existing children instead. Cannot be combined with previousNavigatorItemId.

paperWidth.description: Optional paper width in mm, used together with paperHeight. Sets the size of the new layout, and of the master layout when this command creates it from masterLayoutName: a new master starts with the template's default size, which layoutParameters cannot change. An existing master keeps its size. Wins over layoutParameters.horizontalSize.

paperHeight.description: Optional paper height in mm, used together with paperWidth. See paperWidth. Wins over layoutParameters.verticalSize.

commands.name: CreateLayoutSubset
commands.description: Creates Layout Book subsets.

commands.name: GetLayoutSubsetSettings
commands.description: Gets the settings of existing Layout Book subsets: the same fields CreateLayoutSubset accepts (name, ID prefix, numbering style, ...).

subsetSettings.description: One item per input navigator item, in the same order: the subset's settings with the field names of CreateLayoutSubset, or an error.

commands.name: CreateDrawings
commands.description: Creates Drawing elements on the specified or active layout from navigator items.

name.description: Custom title name of the new Drawing. Giving a name implies nameType CustomName unless nameType is set explicitly.

nameType.description: Defaults to CustomName when name is given, otherwise to the Drawing tool's current default.

scale.description: Scale ratio applied to the drawing relative to its source view (API_DrawingType::ratio). Defaults to 1.0.

angle.description: Rotation angle of the drawing in radians. Defaults to the Drawing tool's current default.

drawingScale.description: The nominal scale of the drawing. Defaults to the Drawing tool's current default.

modelOffset.description: Offset of the model origin within the drawing. Defaults to the Drawing tool's current default.

commands.name: ChangeDrawingLink
commands.description: Relinks a Drawing to a different source navigator item. Archicad has no in-place relink API, so this recreates the Drawing against the new source and deletes the original - the returned elementId is a NEW guid, not the input one. The Drawing Title marker's own position is not preserved (undocumented Archicad limitation). The new source view is made current before the Drawing is created (Archicad 27 or later), and the window and story that were active when the command started are restored afterwards; the view settings (zoom, layers, scale) shown in that window are not restored.

items.description: An existing Drawing and the navigator item it should be relinked to.

elements.description: One result per input item. On success, elementId is the NEW Drawing's identifier - relinking necessarily replaces the element, it cannot keep the original guid.

commands.name: GetLayoutSettings
commands.description: Gets settings of layouts, including their master layout and Layout Info Panel custom data fields.

masterLayoutDatabaseId.description: The database of the master layout of the layout. Not present for master layouts.

masterNavigatorItemId.description: The Layout Book navigator item of the master layout of the layout. Not present for master layouts.

masterLayoutName.description: The name of the master layout of the layout. Not present for master layouts.

commands.name: SetLayoutSettings
commands.description: Sets settings of layouts, including their master layout and Layout Info Panel custom data fields.

masterNavigatorItemId.description: The master layout to assign to the layout, as its Layout Book navigator item. Only layouts can be given a master layout, master layouts cannot.

masterLayoutDatabaseId.description: The master layout to assign to the layout, as its database. Used when masterNavigatorItemId is not given.

masterLayoutName.description: The master layout to assign to the layout, by name. Used when neither masterNavigatorItemId nor masterLayoutDatabaseId is given.

commands.name: GetLayoutCustomScheme
commands.description: Gets the Layout Info Panel custom field definitions (name and key) from Book Settings.

commands.name: GetModelViewOptions
commands.description: Gets all model view options

items.description: Represents the model view options.

commands.name: GetViewSettings
commands.description: Gets the view settings of navigator items

commands.name: SetViewSettings
commands.description: Sets the view settings of navigator items

commands.name: GetActiveGraphicalOverrideCombination
commands.description: Gets the graphic override combination applied to the current window, with its id and name. The response is empty when no combination is applied. This is the combination of the window itself, not the one stored in a saved view (see GetViewSettings). Available from Archicad 30.

outputScheme.description: The graphic override combination applied to the current window. Empty when the current window has no combination applied.

combinationId.description: The identifier of the graphic override combination.

name.description: The name of the graphic override combination. Missing when the combination cannot be read, e.g. it was deleted.

commands.name: SetActiveGraphicalOverrideCombination
commands.description: Applies a graphic override combination, given by id or by name, to the current window. The current window must be a model window (floor plan, section, elevation, 3D, ...). To remove the overrides, apply the project's 'No Overrides' combination. The saved view is not changed (see SetViewSettings for that). Available from Archicad 30.

inputScheme.description: The graphic override combination to apply, given by id or by name.

combinationId.description: The identifier of the graphic override combination, as returned by GetActiveGraphicalOverrideCombination.

name.description: The name of the graphic override combination, as shown in Document > Graphic Overrides > Graphic Override Combinations.

commands.name: GetStructureDisplay
commands.description: Gets the Partial Structure Display (EntireStructure, CoreOnly, WithoutFinishes or StructureOnly) of the current window, and whether it is the 3D window. This is the setting of the window itself, not the one stored in a saved view (see GetViewSettings). Available from Archicad 27.

outputScheme.description: The Partial Structure Display of the current window.

structureDisplay.description: The Partial Structure Display mode of the current window.

is3D.description: True when the setting belongs to the 3D window.

commands.name: SetStructureDisplay
commands.description: Sets the Partial Structure Display (EntireStructure, CoreOnly, WithoutFinishes or StructureOnly) of the current window, e.g. the floor plan, a section or the 3D window. The change cannot be undone. The saved view is not changed (see SetViewSettings for that). Available from Archicad 27.

structureDisplay.description: The Partial Structure Display mode to apply to the current window.

commands.name: GetView2DTransformations
commands.description: Get zoom and rotation of 2D views

commands.name: SetViewRotation
commands.description: Set the rotation angle of 2D views via their floor plan database.

commands.name: CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap
