commands.description: Clones Project Map viewpoints into a specified View Map folder.

viewsData.description: Array of views to clone from the Project Map to the View Map.

navigatorItemId.description: Navigator item ID of the Project Map viewpoint to clone.

parentNavigatorItemId.description: Navigator item ID of the View Map folder to place the clone in. Required - Archicad's CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap API leaves a clone created directly at the View Map root in a broken state (it cannot be deleted or moved afterwards, by API or by hand), so Tapir refuses to fall back to the root on your behalf. Create a View Map folder (CreateViewMapFolder) first if you don't already have one to target.

commands.name: CreateViewsInViewMap
commands.description: Creates independent (non-clone) navigator views in a specified View Map folder, by copying database and settings from source items.

viewsData.description: Array of views to create as independent (non-clone) items in the View Map.

navigatorItemId.description: Source navigator item whose database and settings are copied.

parentNavigatorItemId.description: View Map folder to place the new view in. Required - the underlying Archicad API used to create the item leaves it undeletable and unmovable afterwards when it is attached directly to the View Map root, so Tapir refuses to fall back to the root on your behalf. Create a View Map folder (CreateViewMapFolder) first if you don't already have one to target.

name.description: Name for the new view. Optional; defaults to the source item name.

commands.name: CreateViewMapFolder
commands.description: Creates a new folder in the View Map.

folderName.description: Name of the new folder to create in the View Map.

parentNavigatorItemId.description: Navigator item ID of the parent View Map folder. Optional; defaults to the View Map root.

commands.name: Set3DCutPlanes
commands.description: Sets the 3D cut planes. An empty cutPlanes array switches the 3D cut off.

cutPlanes.description: The cut planes. An empty array switches the 3D cut off. The side of a plane its normal vector points to is cut away and the other side is kept (to be confirmed in Archicad). pd is in meters.

items.description: Defines a 3D cut plane using the plane equation: pa*x + pb*y + pc*z + pd = 0

pa.description: Coefficient of x in the plane equation. The x coordinate of the normal vector of the plane.

pb.description: Coefficient of y in the plane equation. The y coordinate of the normal vector of the plane.

pc.description: Coefficient of z in the plane equation. The z coordinate of the normal vector of the plane.

pd.description: Constant term in the plane equation, in meters. The distance of the plane from the origin along the normal vector.

commands.name: Get3DCutPlanes
commands.description: Gets whether the 3D cut planes are on and the cut planes (pa, pb, pc, pd) of the 3D window, in the form accepted by Set3DCutPlanes.

isCutPlanes.description: Whether the 3D cut planes are switched on.

useCustom.description: Whether the custom cut settings are used.

cutPlanes.description: The cut planes, in the form accepted by Set3DCutPlanes: pa*x + pb*y + pc*z + pd = 0, pd in meters.

commands.name: Get3DStyleDetails
commands.description: Gets the settings of 3D styles by name (an empty name or no names means the current 3D style): rendering engine, model type, monochrome and background colors, contours, shadows and hatching. Available from Archicad 27.

names.description: The names of the 3D styles. An empty name means the current 3D style. When omitted, the current 3D style is returned.

styles.description: The details of the 3D styles, in the order of the input names.

name.description: The name of the 3D style, unique within the project.

engineId.description: The id of the 3D rendering engine (API_3DStyle.engineId).

model3D.description: The 3D model type: Block, Wireframe, Hidden Line or Shading, as the integer value of API_3DModelTypeID.

monochromeEnabled.description: The model is shown in monochrome colors.

monochromeSurfaceColor.description: The surface color of the monochrome model.

monochromeContourColor.description: The contour color of the monochrome model.

backgroundAsInRendering.description: The background is the same as in the rendering settings.

chainBackgroundColors.description: The sky and the ground background colors are chained.

backgroundSkyColor.description: The sky color of the background (API_3DStyle.bkgSkyColor).

shadingContours.description: The contours in shaded mode, as the integer value of API_ShadingContoursID.

vectorialSunShadow.description: The vectorial sun shadow options, as the integer value of API_VectorShadowID.

contourThickness.description: The thickness of the contours, in pixels.

silhouetteThickness.description: The thickness of the silhouettes, in pixels.

vectorialHatchingThickness.description: The thickness of the vectorial hatching, in pixels.

shadowContourThickness.description: The thickness of the shadow contours, in pixels.

castShadowPercent.description: The intensity of the cast shadows, in percent.

shadingPercent.description: The intensity of the shading, in percent.

shadowElevation.description: The elevation of the shadow plane, used by the one level vectorial sun shadow options.

commands.name: Create3DStyles
commands.description: Creates 3D styles. Each new style starts from the current 3D style and differs from it only in the given fields. Available from Archicad 27.

styles.description: The 3D styles to create. Each starts from the current 3D style; only the given fields differ from it.

name.description: The name of the 3D style, unique within the project.

engineId.description: The id of the 3D rendering engine (API_3DStyle.engineId).

model3D.description: The 3D model type: Block, Wireframe, Hidden Line or Shading, as the integer value of API_3DModelTypeID.

monochromeEnabled.description: The model is shown in monochrome colors.

monochromeSurfaceColor.description: The surface color of the monochrome model.

monochromeContourColor.description: The contour color of the monochrome model.

backgroundAsInRendering.description: The background is the same as in the rendering settings.

chainBackgroundColors.description: The sky and the ground background colors are chained.

backgroundSkyColor.description: The sky color of the background (API_3DStyle.bkgSkyColor).

shadingContours.description: The contours in shaded mode, as the integer value of API_ShadingContoursID.

vectorialSunShadow.description: The vectorial sun shadow options, as the integer value of API_VectorShadowID.

contourThickness.description: The thickness of the contours, in pixels.

silhouetteThickness.description: The thickness of the silhouettes, in pixels.

vectorialHatchingThickness.description: The thickness of the vectorial hatching, in pixels.

shadowContourThickness.description: The thickness of the shadow contours, in pixels.

castShadowPercent.description: The intensity of the cast shadows, in percent.

shadingPercent.description: The intensity of the shading, in percent.

shadowElevation.description: The elevation of the shadow plane, used by the one level vectorial sun shadow options.

commands.name: Change3DStyles
commands.description: Changes the given fields of existing 3D styles, identified by name. Available from Archicad 27.

styles.description: The 3D styles to change, identified by their name. Only the given fields change.

name.description: The name of the 3D style, unique within the project.

engineId.description: The id of the 3D rendering engine (API_3DStyle.engineId).

model3D.description: The 3D model type: Block, Wireframe, Hidden Line or Shading, as the integer value of API_3DModelTypeID.

monochromeEnabled.description: The model is shown in monochrome colors.

monochromeSurfaceColor.description: The surface color of the monochrome model.

monochromeContourColor.description: The contour color of the monochrome model.

backgroundAsInRendering.description: The background is the same as in the rendering settings.

chainBackgroundColors.description: The sky and the ground background colors are chained.

backgroundSkyColor.description: The sky color of the background (API_3DStyle.bkgSkyColor).

shadingContours.description: The contours in shaded mode, as the integer value of API_ShadingContoursID.

vectorialSunShadow.description: The vectorial sun shadow options, as the integer value of API_VectorShadowID.

contourThickness.description: The thickness of the contours, in pixels.

silhouetteThickness.description: The thickness of the silhouettes, in pixels.

vectorialHatchingThickness.description: The thickness of the vectorial hatching, in pixels.

shadowContourThickness.description: The thickness of the shadow contours, in pixels.

castShadowPercent.description: The intensity of the cast shadows, in percent.

shadingPercent.description: The intensity of the shading, in percent.

shadowElevation.description: The elevation of the shadow plane, used by the one level vectorial sun shadow options.

commands.name: Get3DProjectionSettings
commands.description: Gets the 3D projection settings of the 3D window: whether it is perspective or axonometric, the camera and target position, view cone, roll angle, distance and azimuth of a perspective, or the transformation matrix of an axonometry.

isPersp.description: True for a perspective projection, false for an axonometric one.

cameraElementId.description: The Camera element the projection was set from. Missing when the projection does not come from a camera.

activeCameraSetElementId.description: The active Camera Set element. Missing when there is none.

perspective.description: The perspective parameters. Present only when isPersp is true.

axonometric.description: The parameters of an axonometric projection. Present only when isPersp is false.

transformationMatrix.description: The 3x4 transformation matrix of the axonometric projection, row by row (12 numbers).

commands.name: Set3DProjectionSettings
commands.description: Sets a perspective projection for the 3D window. Every perspective parameter is required: read a known good set with Get3DProjectionSettings and pass it back, with the values to change replaced.

commands.name: Get3DWindowSettings
commands.description: Gets the 3D window settings: the pixel size of the 3D window and the zoom (scale and displacement) of its projection.

hSize.description: The horizontal size of the 3D window in pixels.

vSize.description: The vertical size of the 3D window in pixels.

zoomScaleX.description: The horizontal zoom scale of the 3D projection.

zoomScaleY.description: The vertical zoom scale of the 3D projection.

zoomDispX.description: The horizontal displacement (pan) of the 3D projection.

zoomDispY.description: The vertical displacement (pan) of the 3D projection.

commands.name: Set3DWindowSettings
commands.description: Changes the pixel size of the 3D window and/or the zoom (scale and displacement) of its projection; the values not given are kept. Returns the settings read back after the change. Archicad may need a rebuild of the 3D window (RebuildView) before it shows the change, e.g. before SaveCurrentWindowAsImage.

hSize.description: The horizontal size of the 3D window in pixels.

vSize.description: The vertical size of the 3D window in pixels.

zoomScaleX.description: The horizontal zoom scale of the 3D projection.

zoomScaleY.description: The vertical zoom scale of the 3D projection.

zoomDispX.description: The horizontal displacement (pan) of the 3D projection.

zoomDispY.description: The vertical displacement (pan) of the 3D projection.

hSize.description: The horizontal size of the 3D window in pixels.

vSize.description: The vertical size of the 3D window in pixels.

zoomScaleX.description: The horizontal zoom scale of the 3D projection.

zoomScaleY.description: The vertical zoom scale of the 3D projection.

zoomDispX.description: The horizontal displacement (pan) of the 3D projection.

zoomDispY.description: The vertical displacement (pan) of the 3D projection.

commands.name: FitInWindow
commands.description: Zooms to the given elements or fits everything in the window.

commands.name: SetZoom
commands.description: Zooms the current 2D window to the given box in model coordinates.

zoomBox.description: The area to zoom the current 2D window to, in model coordinates (meters). The window keeps its aspect ratio, so the shown area may be larger than the box.

commands.name: ResetZoom
commands.description: Steps back in the zoom history of the current window, like Archicad's Zoom Back.

numberOfStepsBack.description: The number of steps to go back in the zoom history of the current window, like Archicad's Zoom Back. The default is 1.

commands.name: CreateSections
commands.description: Creates Section elements on the floor plan.

commands.name: CreateInteriorElevations
commands.description: Creates Interior Elevation elements on the floor plan. Every consecutive pair of the given points becomes one segment, each with its own viewpoint - feed it the corner points of a room to get an interior elevation of that room.

interiorElevationsData.description: Array of data to create Interior Elevation elements.

commands.name: MoveNavigatorItem
commands.description: Moves a navigator item to a new parent in the navigator tree.

commands.name: RenameNavigatorItem
commands.description: Renames a navigator item or changes its ID. newId sets the custom layout number of a layout and the custom ID of any other item. Fails when Archicad refuses the change or does not apply the new name or ID (e.g. Project Map items, whose schedule items are named by their scheme). With customName false the item drops its custom name and follows its Project Map source again.

newId.description: The new ID of the item. On a layout it is the custom layout number (customLayoutNumbering is switched on); on any other item it is the custom ID of the navigator item (customUiId becomes true).

customName.description: Set to false to drop the custom name of the item, so that it follows the name of its Project Map source again. Cannot be combined with newName.

commands.name: DeleteNavigatorItems
commands.description: Deletes navigator items from the navigator tree: views and folders of the View Map, layouts and master layouts of the Layout Book, and independent worksheets and details of the Project Map. Layout subsets and marker-linked worksheets and details cannot be deleted.

commands.name: GetNavigatorItemTree
commands.description: Returns the full navigator item tree for the specified map. With includeChildCount true every item also reports the number of its direct children.

publisherSetName.description: The name of the publisher set to retrieve. Used only when navigatorMapId is PublisherSets. Without it the first publisher set is returned.

includeChildCount.description: Set to true to add childCount, the number of direct children Archicad reports, to every item. Defaults to false.

commands.name: GetNavigatorParentItems
commands.description: Returns the parent of each given navigator item: the folder, subset or layout book item it is in. The root of a map has no parent and gets an error.

parentItems.description: The parent of each requested navigator item, in the order of the input, or an error for an item whose parent cannot be read.

name.description: The name of the parent navigator item.

commands.name: CreateGraphicalOverrideRule
commands.description: Creates or overwrites a graphic override rule in a rule group: name, criterion XML, surface color and line pen. Needs Archicad 27 or later.

name.description: Name of the override rule. Rule names are unique in the project: an existing rule with this name is overwritten, in whichever rule group it is.

ruleGroupName.description: Rule group of a new rule, created when it does not exist. Default: 'Tapir'. An overwritten rule stays in its own group.

criterionXML.description: Optional criterion XML. Archicad only takes XML in its own format: read it from a rule made in the GUI with GetGraphicalOverrideRules and change the values. XML written from scratch is dropped without an error, and so is an empty one: the rule then applies to all elements.

surfaceRGB.description: Optional color override of the cut and uncut surfaces. Components are in the 0..1 range.

linePenIndex.description: Optional pen index override for lines, markers and texts. Only a positive index takes effect.

overrideContours.description: Optional. If true, the contours of the overridden surfaces are recolored too.

ruleId.description: The created or overwritten override rule.

commands.name: GetGraphicalOverrideRules
commands.description: Returns every graphic override rule with its criterion XML. Needs Archicad 27 or later.

ruleGroupName.description: Name of the rule group the rule belongs to.

criterionXML.description: The criterion in Archicad's own XML format. Change its values and pass it to CreateGraphicalOverrideRule to make similar rules.

commands.name: CreateGraphicalOverrideCombination
commands.description: Creates a graphic override combination from rule names, or replaces the rules of an existing one. Needs Archicad 27 or later.

name.description: Name of the override combination. When a combination with this name exists, its rule list is replaced.

ruleNames.description: Names of the override rules in the combination, in order. Rule names are unique in the project, whatever the rule group. An empty list makes a combination without rules.

combinationId.description: The created or changed override combination.

commands.name: CreateIssue
commands.description: Creates a new issue.

name.description: The name of the issue.

tagText.description: Tag text of the issue, optional.

commands.name: DeleteIssue
commands.description: Deletes the specified issue.

acceptAllElements.description: Accept all creation/deletion/modification of the deleted issue. By default false.

commands.name: GetIssues
commands.description: Retrieves information about existing issues.

name.description: Issue name

isTagTextElemVisible.description: The visibility of the attached tag text element

commands.name: AddCommentToIssue
commands.description: Adds a new comment to the specified issue.

author.description: The author of the new comment.

commands.name: GetCommentsFromIssue
commands.description: Retrieves comments information from the specified issue.

commands.name: AttachElementsToIssue
commands.description: Attaches elements to the specified issue.

commands.name: DetachElementsFromIssue
commands.description: Detaches elements from the specified issue.

commands.name: GetElementsAttachedToIssue
commands.description: Retrieves attached elements of the specified issue, filtered by attachment type.

commands.name: ExportIssuesToBCF
commands.description: Exports specified issues to a BCF file.

issues.description: Leave it empty to export all issues.

exportPath.description: The os path to the bcf file, including it's name.

useExternalId.description: Use external IFC ID or Archicad IFC ID as referenced in BCF topics.

alignBySurveyPoint.description: Align BCF views by Archicad Survey Point or Archicad Project Origin.

commands.name: ImportIssuesFromBCF
commands.description: Imports issues from the specified BCF file.

importPath.description: The os path to the bcf file, including it's name.

alignBySurveyPoint.description: Align BCF views by Archicad Survey Point or Archicad Project Origin.

commands.name: ImportMarkupsFromPDF
commands.description: Imports the markups of the specified PDF file as issues, like Issue Manager > Import PDF markups, without any dialog and without opening the Issue Manager palette, and reports the issues it created. Available from Archicad 29.

pdfFilePath.description: The os path to the PDF file with the markups, including it's name.

issues.description: The issues the import created. Empty when the import failed.

commands.name: GetRevisionIssues
commands.description: Retrieves all issues.

commands.name: GetRevisionChanges
commands.description: Retrieves all changes.

commands.name: GetRevisionChangeCustomScheme
commands.description: Retrieves the custom fields of changes (the change custom scheme): the key and the name of each field. The keys are the customSchemeKey values in the customSchemeData of changes.

customSchemeKey.description: The identifier of the custom field. The same key is used in the customSchemeData of the revision changes.

customSchemeName.description: The name of the custom field.

commands.name: GetDocumentRevisions
commands.description: Retrieves all document revisions.

commands.name: GetCurrentRevisionChangesOfLayouts
commands.description: Retrieves all changes belong to the last revision of the given layouts.

commands.name: GetRevisionChangesOfElements
commands.description: Retrieves the changes belong to the given elements.

commands.name: GetDesignOptions
commands.description: Retrieves information about existing design options. Available from Archicad 29.

commands.name: GetDesignOptionSets
commands.description: Retrieves information about existing design option sets, and in Teamwork projects the Teamwork identifier of the design options. Available from Archicad 29.

designOptionSetId.description: The guid identifier of the design option set.

name.description: The name of the design option set.

designOptions.description: The list of design options in the set.

teamworkId.description: The Teamwork identifier of the project's design options. Present only in Teamwork projects.

commands.name: GetDesignOptionCombinations
commands.description: Retrieves information about existing design option combinations.

commands.name: GetElementsOfDesignOptions
commands.description: Retrieves the elements associated with the given design options. Available from Archicad 29.

commands.name: GetDesignOptionForElements
commands.description: Retrieves the design option association for the specified elements. Available from Archicad 29.

commands.name: CreateDesignOptionSets
commands.description: Creates new design option sets with the given names. Available from Archicad 29.

commands.name: CreateDesignOptions
commands.description: Creates new design options with the given parameters. Available from Archicad 29.

commands.name: CreateDesignOptionCombinations
commands.description: Creates new design option combinations with the given parameters. Available from Archicad 29.

commands.name: SetActiveDesignOptionsInCombinations
commands.description: Sets active design options in the given combinations. Available from Archicad 29.

activeDesignOptions.description: The list of active design options in the combination.

commands.name: DeactivateDesignOptionsInCombinations
commands.description: Turns off the given design options in the given combinations, leaving their other options as they are. Available from Archicad 29.

designOptions.description: The design options to turn off in the combination. The other options of the combination are left as they are.

commands.name: MoveElementsToDesignOptions
commands.description: Moves the given elements into the given design options. Use NULLGuid for design option to remove the element from any design options and move it to the main model. Available from Archicad 29.

designOptionId.description: The identifier of the design option to move the element into. Use NULLGuid to remove the element from any design option and move it to the main model.

commands.name: MoveDesignOptionsToAnotherSet
commands.description: Moves the given design options to another sets. Available from Archicad 29.

designOptionId.description: The identifier of the design option to move.

commands.name: RenameDesignOptions
commands.description: Changes the name and/or the string id of the given design options. Available from Archicad 29.

name.description: The new name of the design option. The name is kept when it is not given.

id.description: The new string id of the design option. The id is kept when it is not given.

designOptions.description: The design options to rename, each with the new name and/or id. At least one of them must be given.

commands.name: RenameDesignOptionSets
commands.description: Changes the name of the given design option sets. Available from Archicad 29.

name.description: The new name of the design option set.

designOptionSets.description: The design option sets to rename, each with the new name.

commands.name: RenameDesignOptionCombinations
commands.description: Changes the name of the given design option combinations. Available from Archicad 29.

name.description: The new name of the design option combination.

designOptionCombinations.description: The design option combinations to rename, each with the new name.

commands.name: DeleteDesignOptions
commands.description: Deletes the given design options. Available from Archicad 29.

commands.name: DeleteDesignOptionSets
commands.description: Deletes the given design option sets. Available from Archicad 29.

designOptionSets.description: The design option sets to delete.

commands.name: DeleteDesignOptionCombinations
commands.description: Deletes the given design option combinations. Available from Archicad 29.

designOptionCombinations.description: The design option combinations to delete.

commands.name: DuplicateDesignOptionCombinations
commands.description: Duplicates the given design option combinations and returns the identifiers of the new combinations. Available from Archicad 29.

designOptionCombinations.description: The design option combinations to duplicate.

designOptionCombinationIdsOrErrors.description: The identifiers of the new combinations, in the order of the input, or an error for each combination that could not be duplicated.

commands.name: GetKeynoteTree
commands.description: Retrieves the whole keynote folder and item hierarchy. The technical root folder is not included in the output; the top-level folders and items are returned directly. Available from Archicad 28.

foldersInRoot.description: The top-level keynote folders with their content recursively. The technical root folder itself is not included.

itemsInRoot.description: The keynote items located directly in the technical root folder.

commands.name: GetKeynoteAutoTexts
commands.description: Retrieves the autotext tokens of the given keynote items. The tokens can be used as label text content to reference the fields of a keynote item. Available from Archicad 28.

keynoteItems.description: The keynote items to get the autotext tokens for.

commands.name: CreateKeynoteFolders
commands.description: Creates keynote folders under the given parent folders (or under the root folder). Available from Archicad 28.

foldersData.description: Array of data to create keynote folders.

parentFolderId.description: The parent folder. Optional; defaults to the root folder.

commands.name: CreateKeynoteItems
commands.description: Creates keynote items in the given parent folders (or in the root folder). Available from Archicad 28.

itemsData.description: Array of data to create keynote items.

parentFolderId.description: The parent folder. Optional; defaults to the root folder.

commands.name: ModifyKeynoteFolders
commands.description: Modifies the key, title or reference of the given keynote folders. Available from Archicad 28.

foldersData.description: Array of data to modify keynote folders. Only provided fields are changed.

commands.name: ModifyKeynoteItems
commands.description: Modifies the key, title, description or reference of the given keynote items. Available from Archicad 28.

itemsData.description: Array of data to modify keynote items. Only provided fields are changed.

commands.name: DeleteKeynoteFolders
commands.description: Deletes the given keynote folders including their content. Available from Archicad 28.

commands.name: DeleteKeynoteItems
commands.description: Deletes the given keynote items. Available from Archicad 28.

commands.name: CreateKeynoteLabels
commands.description: Creates Label elements that reference the given keynote items via autotext. Available from Archicad 28.

labelsData.description: Array of data to create keynote labels.

position.description: The reference point of the label.

contentFields.description: The keynote fields to include in the label text as autotext. Optional; defaults to all fields.

commands.name: GetProjectDataKeys
commands.description: Lists the project data stored by Tapir in the project: the names, the identifiers of the add-on objects that store them, whether they are kept on this client only and the Teamwork user who has reserved them. Project data is text (for example JSON) saved in the project file by scripts and Grasshopper definitions, such as their settings or the mapping of elements to an external system.

keys.description: The project data stored by Tapir in the project.

name.description: The name of the project data.

guid.description: The identifier of the add-on object that stores the project data.

clientOnly.description: True when the project data is kept on this client only and is not shared in Teamwork.

teamworkOwner.description: The Teamwork user who has reserved the project data. Omitted when nobody has reserved it or the project is not a Teamwork project.

commands.name: GetProjectData
commands.description: Gets the content of the project data with the given names.

names.description: The names of the project data to get.

values.description: The project data in the order of the given names, or an error for a name that has no project data.

name.description: The name of the project data.

content.description: The content of the project data.

commands.name: SetProjectData
commands.description: Creates or overwrites project data: text (for example JSON) saved in the project under a name. New project data can be kept on this client only, or created as unique so that in Teamwork only one can exist with its name. Prefix the names with the name of your tool (for example 'my-tool/settings') so scripts do not overwrite each other's data.

values.description: The project data to create or to overwrite. Prefix the names with the name of your tool (for example 'my-tool/settings') so different scripts do not overwrite each other's data.

name.description: The name of the project data.

content.description: The content of the project data, for example a JSON string.

clientOnly.description: Creates the project data on this client only, it is not shared in Teamwork. Used only when the project data is created. The default is false.

unique.description: Creates the project data as a unique add-on object: in Teamwork only one can exist with its name, even when several users create it at the same time. Used only when the project data is created, and cannot be combined with clientOnly. The default is false.

commands.name: DeleteProjectData
commands.description: Deletes the project data with the given names.

names.description: The names of the project data to delete.

commands.name: ReserveProjectData
commands.description: Reserves the project data with the given names in Teamwork, so that other users cannot change it. Returns the users who have already reserved some of it.

names.description: The names of the project data to reserve.

conflicts.description: The project data that could not be reserved because another user has reserved it.

name.description: The name of the project data.

commands.name: ReleaseProjectData
commands.description: Releases the project data with the given names in Teamwork.

names.description: The names of the project data to release.

commands.name: RequestProjectData
commands.description: Requests the project data with the given names in Teamwork from the users who have reserved it, with an optional message.

names.description: The names of the project data to request from the users who have reserved them.

mailText.description: The message sent with the request. The default is empty.

commands.name: GrantProjectData
commands.description: Grants the project data with the given names, reserved by the current user, to another Teamwork user.

names.description: The names of the project data, reserved by the current user, to grant.

toUserId.description: The Teamwork user id of the user who gets the project data, for example the userId of a user returned by GetProjectDataKeys or ReserveProjectData.

commands.name: GetMEPElements
commands.description: Retrieves the MEP (Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing) elements of the project, optionally filtered by type and domain. MEP elements are ordinary elements, so the generic element commands work on them as well (for example they can be deleted with the DeleteElements command). Available from Archicad 28.

elementTypes.description: Optional filter for the MEP element types.

domains.description: Optional filter for the MEP domains.

elements.description: The MEP elements.

commands.name: GetMEPRoutingElements
commands.description: Retrieves the details of the given MEP routing elements: domain, MEP system, offset from the home story, branch preference table, the ports logically connected at the route's beginning and end, route polyline, segments with cross section data (shape, size, preference table and reference id), begin and end nodes, anchor, reference line offsets, wall thickness, flange size and rigid segments, and nodes with their incoming and outgoing segments, elbows and transitions. Available from Archicad 28.

commands.name: GetMEPPorts
commands.description: Retrieves the ports of the given MEP elements including position, shape, size and connection status. Available from Archicad 28.

commands.name: GetMEPDistributionSystems
commands.description: Retrieves the MEP distribution systems of the project with their domain, MEP system attribute and member elements. Available from Archicad 28.

distributionSystems.description: The distribution systems of the project.

commands.name: CreateMEPRoutingElements
commands.description: Creates MEP routing elements (duct, pipe or cable carrier routes) along the given polylines with optional cross section data (shape, size, preference table and reference id), MEP system and layer (also set on the segments, elbows and transitions). Available from Archicad 28.

routingElementsData.description: Array of data to create MEP routing elements.

nodeCoordinates.description: The corner points of the route polyline.

crossSectionWidth.description: Optional cross section width applied to all segments.

crossSectionHeight.description: Optional cross section height applied to all segments.

crossSectionReferenceId.description: Optional cross section reference id of the segment preference table (used for circular cross sections). Resolved against preferenceTableId if given, otherwise against the table of the current routing tool default.

preferenceTableId.description: Optional guid of the segment preference table (see GetMEPPreferenceTables) applied to all segments. Not applicable to the CableCarrier domain.

layerIndex.description: Optional layer attribute index of the routing element and all its parts (routing segments, rigid segments, elbows and transitions). Only a positive index takes effect; otherwise the routing tool default layer is used. A layer that does not exist or is locked gives an error for the item, and nothing is placed.

commands.name: CreateMEPElements
commands.description: Creates MEP elements (Terminal, Accessory, Equipment or Fitting) at the given positions. Available from Archicad 28.

elementsData.description: Array of data to create MEP elements.

domain.description: Required for all types except Equipment.

orientationDirection.description: Optional direction vector of the orientation. Defaults to (1, 0, 0).

orientationRotation.description: Optional rotation vector of the orientation. Defaults to (0, 1, 0).

commands.name: ModifyMEPRoutingElements
commands.description: Modifies the given MEP routing elements: MEP system, branch preference table, cross section data (shape, size, preference table and reference id), anchor, reference line offsets, wall thickness and flange size of all segments, and node positions. Available from Archicad 28.

routingElementsData.description: Array of data to modify MEP routing elements. Only provided fields are changed.

crossSectionWidth.description: New cross section width applied to all segments.

crossSectionHeight.description: New cross section height applied to all segments.

crossSectionShape.description: The new shape is applied to all segments.

crossSectionReferenceId.description: New cross section reference id of the segment preference table applied to all segments (used for circular cross sections). Resolved against preferenceTableId if given, otherwise against the table the segments already use.

preferenceTableId.description: New segment preference table (guid as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables) applied to all segments. Not applicable to the CableCarrier domain.

branchPreferenceTableId.description: New branch preference table (guid as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables) of the routing element.

anchor.description: New anchor point of the cross section, on a 3x3 grid, applied to all segments.

referenceLineOffsetX.description: New horizontal offset of the reference line from the anchor point, applied to all segments.

referenceLineOffsetY.description: New vertical offset of the reference line from the anchor point, applied to all segments.

wallThickness.description: New wall thickness applied to all segments.

flangeSize.description: New flange size applied to all segments.

nodePositions.description: New positions of the routing nodes. The size must match the number of nodes of the route.

commands.name: ConnectMEPElements
commands.description: Connects MEP routing elements to other MEP elements or routes. Merges routes, splits routes or creates branch elements as needed. Available from Archicad 28.

connectToId.description: The MEP element or routing element to connect to.

commands.name: GetMEPPreferenceTables
commands.description: Gets the circular cross section preference tables (referenceId, diameter, description) and the reference set of the Piping or Ventilation domain, optionally with the elbow, branch and transition preference tables. The angle set and the transition tables are available from Archicad 29. Available from Archicad 28.

includeFittingTables.description: Also return the elbow, branch and transition preference tables. Defaults to false.

tables.description: The circular segment preference tables of the domain.

elbowTables.description: The elbow preference tables of the domain. Only when includeFittingTables is true.

branchTables.description: The branch preference tables of the domain. Only when includeFittingTables is true.

transitionTables.description: The transition preference tables of the domain. Only when includeFittingTables is true, available from Archicad 29.

commands.name: GetMEPSystemGroups
commands.description: Gets the MEP system groups of the project with their physical systems: name, editable flag, root element and MEP system. Available from Archicad 29.

systemGroups.description: The system groups of the project with their physical systems.

commands.name: CreateMEPSystemGroups
commands.description: Creates MEP system groups. Available from Archicad 29.

systemGroupsData.description: Array of data to create system groups.

commands.name: CreateMEPPhysicalSystems
commands.description: Creates physical systems in MEP system groups, optionally with a root element and an MEP system as their category. Available from Archicad 29.

physicalSystemsData.description: Array of data to create physical systems.

systemGroupId.description: The system group the new physical system belongs to.

rootElementId.description: The MEP element the system starts from. Archicad keeps it only while it is part of an MEP network: the root of a stand-alone element is cleared when the MEP networks are recalculated.

mepSystemId.description: The MEP system attribute used as the category of the physical system.

commands.name: ModifyMEPSystemGroups
commands.description: Renames MEP system groups. Available from Archicad 29.

systemGroupsData.description: Array of data to modify system groups.

name.description: The new name of the system group.

commands.name: ModifyMEPPhysicalSystems
commands.description: Modifies MEP physical systems: name, root element and the MEP system used as their category. Only the given fields are changed. Available from Archicad 29.

physicalSystemsData.description: Array of data to modify physical systems. Only the given fields are changed.

name.description: The new name of the physical system.

rootElementId.description: The MEP element the system starts from. Archicad keeps it only while it is part of an MEP network: the root of a stand-alone element is cleared when the MEP networks are recalculated.

mepSystemId.description: The MEP system attribute used as the category of the physical system.

commands.name: DeleteMEPPhysicalSystems
commands.description: Removes MEP physical systems from their system groups. Their member elements are not deleted. Available from Archicad 29.

physicalSystems.description: The physical systems to remove from their system groups. Their member elements are not deleted.

commands.name: GetElectricalPanels
commands.description: Gets the electrical panels (distribution boards) of the project or the given ones: name, circuit naming, circuits, parent circuit, placement and the connected and demand loads in total and per phase. Available from Archicad 30.

elements.description: Optional list of electrical panels. Every electrical panel of the project is returned when it is not given.

electricalPanels.description: The electrical panels, in the order of the given elements.

commands.name: GetElectricalCircuits
commands.description: Gets the given electrical circuits, the circuits of the given panels, or every circuit of the project: name, description, owner panel, connected devices and panels, voltage, phases, wiring type, loads, voltage drop and estimated cable length. Available from Archicad 30.

elements.description: Optional list of electrical circuits.

electricalPanels.description: Optional list of electrical panels whose circuits are returned. When neither elements nor electricalPanels is given, every circuit of every electrical panel of the project is returned.

electricalCircuits.description: The given circuits first, in their order, then the circuits of the given panels, in the order of the panels.

commands.name: GetElectricalDevices
commands.description: Gets the electrical devices (lights, sockets and other consumers) of the project or the given ones: parent circuit, placement, apparent power, load classification, demand load and directly connected MEP elements. Available from Archicad 30.

elements.description: Optional list of electrical devices. Every electrical device of the project is returned when it is not given.

electricalDevices.description: The electrical devices, in the order of the given elements.

commands.name: GetElectricalProjectSettings
commands.description: Gets the electrical project settings: the default voltage, the wiring types with their cross-sectional area and the load classifications with their demand factor. Available from Archicad 30.

voltage.description: The default voltage of the project.

crossSectionalArea.description: The cross-sectional area of the wire in square millimeters.

commands.name: CreateElectricalPanels
commands.description: Places electrical panels with the default settings of the Electrical Panel tool, optionally with the given library part, size, rotation, mirroring, panel name and circuit naming. Available from Archicad 30.

electricalPanelsData.description: Array of data to create electrical panels. The fields that are not given are taken from the default settings of the Electrical Panel tool.

position.description: The anchor point of the new panel.

orientation.description: Defaults to the direction (1, 0, 0) and the rotation (0, 1, 0).

libraryPartId.description: The library part to use, as listed by GetAvailableLibraryParts.

xSize.description: The size along the local x axis. Some library parts calculate their own size, then the item fails.

ySize.description: The size along the local y axis. Some library parts calculate their own size, then the item fails.

commands.name: CreateElectricalDevices
commands.description: Places electrical devices with the default settings of the Electrical Device tool, optionally with the given library part, size, rotation, mirroring, apparent power and load classification, and connects them to a circuit. Available from Archicad 30.

electricalDevicesData.description: Array of data to create electrical devices. The fields that are not given are taken from the default settings of the Electrical Device tool.

position.description: The anchor point of the new device.

orientation.description: Defaults to the direction (1, 0, 0) and the rotation (0, 1, 0).

libraryPartId.description: The library part to use, as listed by GetAvailableLibraryParts.

xSize.description: The size along the local x axis. Some library parts calculate their own size, then the item fails.

ySize.description: The size along the local y axis. Some library parts calculate their own size, then the item fails.

loadClassificationName.description: One of the load classifications of the electrical project settings, or an empty string for none.

circuitId.description: The circuit to connect the new device to.

commands.name: ModifyElectricalPanels
commands.description: Modifies the name, circuit naming and placement (anchor point, orientation, rotation, mirroring, library part, size) of electrical panels. Available from Archicad 30.

electricalPanelsData.description: Array of data to modify electrical panels. Only the given fields are changed.

libraryPartId.description: The library part to use, as listed by GetAvailableLibraryParts.

xSize.description: The size along the local x axis. Some library parts calculate their own size, then the item fails.

ySize.description: The size along the local y axis. Some library parts calculate their own size, then the item fails.

commands.name: CreateElectricalCircuits
commands.description: Adds new circuits to electrical panels, optionally with the given description, voltage, wiring type and used phases. Available from Archicad 30.

electricalCircuitsData.description: Array of data to create electrical circuits. Each item adds one circuit to the given panel.

electricalPanelId.description: The panel to add the new circuit to.

wiringTypeName.description: One of the wiring types of the electrical project settings, or an empty string for none.

commands.name: DeleteElectricalCircuits
commands.description: Removes electrical circuits from their panels. Available from Archicad 30.

electricalCircuits.description: The circuits to remove from their panels.

commands.name: ModifyElectricalCircuits
commands.description: Modifies the description, voltage, wiring type and used phases of electrical circuits. Available from Archicad 30.

electricalCircuitsData.description: Array of data to modify electrical circuits. Only the given fields are changed.

wiringTypeName.description: One of the wiring types of the electrical project settings, or an empty string for none.

commands.name: ModifyElectricalDevices
commands.description: Modifies the apparent power, load classification and placement (anchor point, orientation, rotation, mirroring, library part, size) of electrical devices. Available from Archicad 30.

electricalDevicesData.description: Array of data to modify electrical devices. Only the given fields are changed.

loadClassificationName.description: One of the load classifications of the electrical project settings, or an empty string for none.

libraryPartId.description: The library part to use, as listed by GetAvailableLibraryParts.

xSize.description: The size along the local x axis. Some library parts calculate their own size, then the item fails.

ySize.description: The size along the local y axis. Some library parts calculate their own size, then the item fails.

commands.name: ConnectToElectricalCircuits
commands.description: Connects electrical devices, or panels as sub-panels, to electrical circuits. Available from Archicad 30.

connectionsData.description: Array of electrical devices or panels and the circuits to connect them to. A panel connected to a circuit becomes a sub-panel of the panel of that circuit.

elementId.description: An electrical device or an electrical panel.

circuitId.description: The electrical circuit to connect to.

commands.name: ModifyElectricalProjectSettings
commands.description: Modifies the electrical project settings: sets the default voltage and adds or removes wiring types and load classifications. Available from Archicad 30.

wiringTypesToRemove.description: The names of the wiring types to remove.

loadClassificationsToRemove.description: The names of the load classifications to remove.

commands.name: GetCurrentAnalyticalModel
commands.description: Retrieves the Structural Analytical Model created for the current view. Available from Archicad 27.

analyticalModelId.description: The identifier of the Structural Analytical Model of the current view.

commands.name: UpdateAnalyticalModel
commands.description: Triggers an update of the given Structural Analytical Model, or of the model of the current view when no model is given. Available from Archicad 27.

analyticalModelId.description: The identifier of the Structural Analytical Model to update. The model of the current view is updated when it is omitted.

commands.name: SetAnalyticalGenerationSettingsToNoRule
commands.description: Sets the generation settings of the current Structural Analytical Model to no rules. Available from Archicad 27.

commands.name: GetAnalyticalModelCheckTypeId
commands.description: Retrieves the type identifier of the Structural Analytical Model check. Available from Archicad 29.

modelCheckTypeId.description: The type identifier of the Structural Analytical Model check.

commands.name: CreateSolidElementLinks
commands.description: Creates solid element operation links between target and operator elements.

solidLinks.description: List of solid element operation links to create.

commands.name: RemoveSolidElementLinks
commands.description: Removes solid element operation links between target and operator elements.

solidLinks.description: List of solid element operation links to remove.

commands.name: GetSolidElementLinks
commands.description: Returns solid element operation links for each queried element, grouped by role (target or operator).

elements.description: Elements to query. Returns all solid links where each element is a target or an operator.

solidLinks.description: For each input element, the solid links where it acts as target and where it acts as operator.

commands.name: TrimElements
commands.description: Trims construction elements with a roof or shell: the roofs and shells in the list, or one given trimming element with a trim type.

elements.description: The construction elements to trim. Without trimmingElement the roofs and shells among them do the trimming.

trimmingElement.description: Optional. The roof or shell that trims every element in the list.

trimType.description: Used with trimmingElement; defaults to KeepInside.

commands.name: RemoveElementTrims
commands.description: Removes the trim between an element and the roof or shell trimming it.

elementPairs.description: The trimmed element and the roof or shell trimming it, per pair.

commands.name: GetElementTrims
commands.description: Which roofs and shells trim each queried element, with the trim type, and which elements it trims.

elementTrims.description: One item per queried element, in order. An unknown or deleted element is an error item, so it cannot be mistaken for an element that is simply not trimmed.

commands.name: ShowScriptUI
commands.description: Shows the given HTML content in a native Archicad palette (a tkinter alternative for Python scripts).

htmlContent.description: The full HTML document to display in the Script UI palette.

width.description: Optional palette client width in pixels. Leave unset to keep the current size.

height.description: Optional palette client height in pixels. Leave unset to keep the current size.

title.description: Optional palette window title. Leave unset to keep the current title.

resizable.description: Whether the user can drag-resize the palette. Defaults to true.

zoomEnabled.description: Whether Ctrl+scroll/pinch zooming is allowed in the page. Defaults to true.

zoomLevel.description: Optional initial zoom level (1.0 = 100%). Leave unset to keep the current zoom.

scrollBarsVisible.description: Whether the browser's own scrollbars are shown. Defaults to true.

contextMenuEnabled.description: Whether right-click shows the browser's context menu (e.g. Inspect Element). Defaults to true.

navigationDisabled.description: Prevents the page from navigating away (e.g. clicking a link to another site) once it has loaded. Defaults to false.

allowSelfSignedCertificates.description: Only relevant if htmlContent links to a remote https:// resource with a self-signed certificate. Defaults to false.

clearCookies.description: Deletes all browser cookies before loading htmlContent. Defaults to false.

autoHeight.description: Automatically resizes the palette's height to fit the page content as it changes. Defaults to false.

commands.name: GetScriptUIResult
commands.description: Retrieves and clears the result last submitted from the Script UI palette's page (via window.ACAPI.SubmitResult), if any, and reports whether the palette is still open, so a waiting script can stop when the user closes it.

hasResult.description: True if the Script UI page has submitted a result since the last call.

result.description: The submitted content (as passed to window.ACAPI.SubmitResult). Only present when hasResult is true.

isOpen.description: True while the Script UI palette is open. False before the first ShowScriptUI call and once the user closed the palette with its close box, the page called window.ACAPI.ClosePalette or Archicad closed it; stays true while Archicad only temporarily hides all palettes (e.g. during a modal dialog). Lets a waiting script stop polling when the user closes the palette.

commands.name: GenerateDocumentation
commands.description: Generates files for the documentation. Used by Tapir developers only.

destinationFolder.description: Destination folder for the generated documentation files.

ElementIdOrError.description: An element identifier or an error.

ElementIdsOrErrors.description: A list of element identifiers or errors.

ElementTrims.description: The trims of one element: the roofs and shells trimming it, and the elements it trims.

trimmedBy.description: The roofs and shells trimming this element, with the trim type.

trims.description: The elements this roof or shell trims.

ElementTrimsOrError.description: The trims of one element, or an error.

MEPRoutingSegmentDetails.description: The details of an MEP routing segment.

crossSectionReferenceId.description: The cross section reference id of the segment in its preference table (meaningful for circular cross sections).

preferenceTableId.description: The guid of the segment preference table used by the segment (see GetMEPPreferenceTables).

beginNodeId.description: The routing node at the beginning of the segment.

endNodeId.description: The routing node at the end of the segment.

anchor.description: The anchor point of the cross section, on a 3x3 grid.

referenceLineOffsetX.description: The horizontal offset of the reference line from the anchor point.

referenceLineOffsetY.description: The vertical offset of the reference line from the anchor point.

wallThickness.description: The wall thickness of the segment.

flangeSize.description: The flange size of the segment. Only present when the segment has flanges.

rigidSegments.description: The rigid segments (the straight duct, pipe or cable carrier pieces) of the routing segment.

MEPRoutingNodeDetails.description: The details of an MEP routing node.

incomingSegmentId.description: The routing segment ending at this node. Not present at the beginning of the route.

outgoingSegmentId.description: The routing segment starting at this node. Not present at the end of the route.

elbows.description: The elbows (bends in Archicad 28) at this node.

MEPRoutingElementDetails.description: The details of an MEP routing element.

offsetFromHomeStory.description: The offset of the routing element from its home story.

branchPreferenceTableId.description: The guid of the branch preference table used by the routing element (see GetMEPPreferenceTables). Not present when the routing element has none.

logicallyConnectedPortIdAtRouteBegin.description: The port logically connected to the beginning of the route (see GetMEPPorts). Not present when nothing is connected there.

logicallyConnectedPortIdAtRouteEnd.description: The port logically connected to the end of the route (see GetMEPPorts). Not present when nothing is connected there.

MEPRoutingElementDetailsOrError.description: The details of an MEP routing element or an error.

MEPRoutingElementDetailsOrErrors.description: A list of MEP routing element details or errors.

MEPPortDetails.description: The details of a port of an MEP element.

MEPElementPorts.description: The ports of an MEP element.

MEPElementPortsOrError.description: The ports of an MEP element or an error.

MEPElementPortsOrErrors.description: A list of MEP element ports or errors.

MEPConnectionResult.description: The result of connecting an MEP routing element: the routing element deleted by merging, the routing element created by splitting and the branch element created by the connection.

MEPConnectionResultOrError.description: The result of an MEP connection or an error.

MEPConnectionResultsOrErrors.description: A list of MEP connection results or errors.

SurfaceType.description: The type of a surface material.

AttributeFolder.description: An attribute folder, identified by the type of the attributes it holds and its path from the root folder of that type. Attribute folders exist from Archicad 26.

path.description: The names of the folders from the root folder down to this folder, the root folder itself not included. An empty array is the root folder.

DatabaseIdOrError.description: An Archicad database identifier or an error.

DatabaseIdsOrErrors.description: A list of Archicad database identifiers or errors.

AttributeIdOrError.description: An attribute identifier or an error.

AttributeIdsOrErrors.description: A list of attribute identifiers or errors.

KeynoteFolderId.description: The identifier of a keynote folder.

KeynoteItemId.description: The identifier of a keynote item.

KeynoteFolderIdOrError.description: A keynote folder identifier or an error.

KeynoteFolderIdsOrErrors.description: A list of keynote folder identifiers or errors.

KeynoteItemIdOrError.description: A keynote item identifier or an error.

KeynoteItemIdsOrErrors.description: A list of keynote item identifiers or errors.

KeynoteAutoTextTokens.description: The autotext tokens of a keynote item. A token can be used as the text content of a label to reference the field of the keynote item.

KeynoteAutoTextTokensOrError.description: The autotext tokens of a keynote item or an error.

KeynoteAutoTextTokensOrErrors.description: A list of keynote autotext tokens or errors.

name.description: The autotext's display name, as shown in the Insert Autotext dialog of Archicad.

AutoTextNameOrError.description: The display name of one autotext key, or an error.

AutoTextNamesOrErrors.description: One result per input key, in the same order.

KeynoteItemDetails.description: The details of a keynote item.

KeynoteFolderDetails.description: The details of a keynote folder, including its subfolders and items recursively.

DesignOptionId.description: The identifier of a design option.

DesignOptionSetId.description: The identifier of a design option set.

LayersOfLayerCombination.description: List of Layers included in the Layer Combination.

attributeId.description: The identifier of the Layer attribute.

isHidden.description: Visibility of the Layer in the Layer Combination.

isLocked.description: Lock state of the Layer in the Layer Combination.

isWireframe.description: Is wireframe mode forced for the Layer in the Layer Combination.

intersectionGroupNr.description: Intersection group of the Layer in the Layer Combination. Elements on layers having the same group will be intersected.

LayerCombinationAttributeDetails.description: The details of the layer combination attribute.

attributeId.description: The identifier of the layer combination attribute.

attributeIndex.description: The index identifier of the layer combination attribute.

name.description: The name of the layer combination.

LayerCombinationAttributeOrError.description: A layer combination attribute or an error.

LineAttributeOrError.description: A line attribute or an error.

dash.description: Length of the visible part of the item.

gap.description: Length of the invisible part of the item.

FillAttributeOrError.description: A fill attribute or an error.

frequency.description: The distance between two instances of this item.

direction.description: The angle of the item, measured CCW from the horizontal axis, in radians.

offsetLine.description: The parallel offset of the item, measured from the (rotated) horizontal axis.

lineLengths.description: Dash-gap length pairs describing this line item. Must contain an even number of items.

angle.description: Arc angle in radians, measured CCW.

ZoneCategoryAttributeOrError.description: A zone category attribute or an error.

domain.description: The domain(s) this system belongs to. Archicad 29+ allows only one; earlier versions may report several.

materialId.description: The surface (material) attribute applied to the 3D model of the elements of the system.

insulationMaterialId.description: The surface (material) attribute applied to the insulation of the elements of the system.

MEPSystemAttributeOrError.description: An MEP system attribute or an error.

PenTableAttributeOrError.description: A pen table attribute or an error.

skins.description: The profile's skins (hatches), each with its building material/surface/fill, contour and cut-end line settings, and per-edge line data.

ProfileModifier.description: A stretchable edge-offset parameter of the profile, as named by the profile's author in the Profile Editor. Its value is a live geometric measurement matching what the Profile Editor's dimension shows.

name.description: User-authored label, e.g. 'Largeur support'. Present only if the profile's author assigned one.

value.description: Present only when the parameter's dimension anchors could be resolved to concrete positions.

ProfileSkin.description: One skin (hatch) of the profile's cross-section.

skinId.description: Internal identifier of this skin, stable for the lifetime of the profile. Pass it back in CreateProfiles' skinOverrides to target this skin for modification.

outlineCoords.description: The skin's outline polygon vertices, present only when the skinOutlines field is requested alongside skins.

outlineSubPolyEnds.description: Index (into outlineCoords) of the last vertex of each contour, for skins whose outline has holes or multiple contours.

outlineArcs.description: Marks which consecutive outlineCoords pairs are connected by an arc instead of a straight edge.

ProfileEdge.description: One edge of a profile skin's outline.

ProfileAttributeOrError.description: A profile attribute or an error.

CompositeAttributeOrError.description: A composite attribute or an error.

SurfaceAttributeOrError.description: A surface attribute or an error.

LayerAttributeOrError.description: A layer attribute or an error.

BuildingMaterialAttributeOrError.description: A building material attribute or an error.

Guid.description: A Globally Unique Identifier (or Universally Unique Identifier) in its string representation as defined in RFC 4122.

Hotlink.description: The details of a hotlink node.

location.description: The path of the hotlink file.

name.description: The display name of the hotlink node.

instances.description: The hotlink instance elements placed from the node, in the order Archicad returns them - the input of ChangeHotlinkInstances and DeleteElements. Omitted when the node's instances cannot be read.

children.description: The children of the hotlink node if it has any.

HotlinkNodeId.description: The identifier of a hotlink node - the reference to a module source file, which instances are placed from.

HotlinkOrigin.description: Where a hotlink instance's origin lands, in the project's coordinates.

HotlinkDetails.description: Details of a placed hotlink instance: which node it comes from and where it sits.

rotationAngle.description: Counter-clockwise rotation about the origin, in radians.

mirrored.description: True when the module's local X axis is reflected.

existing.description: True when a node for the same source file already existed and was returned instead of created.

HotlinkNodeCreatedOrError.description: The created (or already existing) node's guid, or an error.

PossibleStringValues.description: The possible string values of a GDL parameter.

PossibleNumericValues.description: The possible numeric values of a GDL parameter.

value.description: The numeric value. Present for all flags except 'Step', which instead carries stepBegin/stepValue.

stepBegin.description: Only present when flag is 'Step': the value is stepBegin + n*stepValue for n >= 0.

stepValue.description: Only present when flag is 'Step' - see stepBegin.

name.description: The name of the parameter.

displayName.description: The display name of the parameter.

index.description: The index of the parameter.

dimension1.description: The 1st dimension of array (in case of array value).

dimension2.description: The 2nd dimension of array (in case of array value).

valueDescription.description: The value description for numeric parameter.

isLocked.description: The parameter is locked; i.e. the user cannot modify it

canHaveCustomValue.description: The parameter can have a custom value.

itemDescriptions.description: Per-item text labels for an array-type parameter (API_AddParType.arrayDescriptions), one per array element in dim1xdim2 order. Only present when the library part defines them.

name.description: The name of the parameter.

index1.description: Optional 1-based first index for changing a single item of an array parameter. Only valid for array parameters and only together with a single (non-list) value.

index2.description: Optional 1-based second index for changing a single item of a two-dimensional array parameter. Only valid together with index1. Defaults to 1.

value.description: The new value of the parameter, in the unit GetGDLParametersOfElements reports it in (Angle parameters in radians). For array parameters provide a list of values for one-dimensional arrays (e.g. [1, 2, 3]) or a list of lists for two-dimensional arrays (e.g. [[11, 12], [21, 22]]); the list must contain exactly as many values as the parameter has items, resizing an array parameter is not supported. Alternatively provide index1 (and optionally index2) together with a single value to change one item of the array. Within one command call whole-array (list) values are applied after all single-value changes.

index.description: The index of the parameter.

index1.description: Optional 1-based first index for changing a single item of an array parameter. Only valid for array parameters and only together with a single (non-list) value.

index2.description: Optional 1-based second index for changing a single item of a two-dimensional array parameter. Only valid together with index1. Defaults to 1.

value.description: The new value of the parameter, in the unit GetGDLParametersOfElements reports it in (Angle parameters in radians). For array parameters provide a list of values for one-dimensional arrays (e.g. [1, 2, 3]) or a list of lists for two-dimensional arrays (e.g. [[11, 12], [21, 22]]); the list must contain exactly as many values as the parameter has items, resizing an array parameter is not supported. Alternatively provide index1 (and optionally index2) together with a single value to change one item of the array. Within one command call whole-array (list) values are applied after all single-value changes.

vertexIds.description: Counterclockwise outer-loop vertex indices for this face.

filled.description: Defaults to true. Set to false to create only this loop's edges (a wireframe outline, e.g. a bare rectangle with no surface fill) without an actual face - holes/surfaceId are ignored in that case, since there is no fill for them to apply to.

holes.description: Optional hole loops cut out of this face, each a clockwise list of vertex indices.

surfaceId.description: Optional per-face surface (render material) override. Uses the Morph's default surface when omitted. Ignored during creation in Archicad 25.

coordinates.description: The 3D coordinates of the leveling subline of the mesh.

CurtainWallPattern.description: The column (primary) or row (secondary) pattern of a curtain wall segment: the sizes of the columns/rows of one pattern unit and how the unit is repeated along the segment.

sizes.description: The sizes (widths of the columns or heights of the rows) of the pattern unit in meters, in order from the start of the segment or from the bottom. The unit is repeated to fill the segment.

flexibleIndices.description: Zero-based indices of the columns/rows of the pattern unit that 'BestDivision' may stretch. When omitted, all of them are flexible. Ignored by 'FixedSizes'.

CurtainWallPatternCell.description: The panel and frame classes of one cell of the pattern unit of a curtain wall segment. Panel classes are numbered as Archicad numbers them: 0 is no panel (the cell is left empty), 1 is the first panel class of the curtain wall (as listed in the Curtain Wall Settings, from the favorite or the tool defaults), 2 the second and so on. Frame classes: 0 is no frame (the cell is merged with its neighbour), 1 the Division frame, 2 the Corner frame, 3 the Boundary frame, 4 the first custom frame class of the curtain wall, 5 the second and so on. Fields not given keep the default assignment of the cell.

columnIndex.description: Zero-based column of the cell within the pattern unit, counted from the start of the segment.

rowIndex.description: Zero-based row of the cell within the pattern unit, counted from the bottom.

panelClassIndex.description: The panel class of the cell. 0 leaves the cell without a panel (Archicad keeps a hidden 'deleted panel' subelement there). With a crossing frame it is the class of the left (or lower) half; see rightPanelClassIndex for the other half.

rightPanelClassIndex.description: The panel class of the right (or upper) half of a cell with a crossing frame. Defaults to panelClassIndex.

leftFrameClassIndex.description: The frame class of the frame on the left edge of the cell (the grid line at the start of the column).

bottomFrameClassIndex.description: The frame class of the frame on the bottom edge of the cell (the grid line at the bottom of the row).

crossingFrameClassIndex.description: The frame class of the diagonal frame of the cell. Only used when crossingFrameType is not 'None'.

height.description: Only used for the Rectangular type.

LinkToSettings.description: Mode of linking an element to its home story.

homeStoryDifference.description: Difference of the home story from the current story.

newCreationMode.description: Controls home-story selection during element creation. If true, homeStoryDifference selects the home story relative to the current story and the element's absolute floor index is ignored. If false, the absolute floor index is used and Archicad fills homeStoryDifference. This is a creation instruction, not a persistent linking mode.

CoverFillOrientation.description: Orientation/distortion of the floor plan cover fill.

origo.description: Origin of the fill relative to the project origin.

matrix00.description: X component of the primary distortion (direction) vector - the cosine of the fill angle, if not distorted.

matrix10.description: Y component of the primary distortion (direction) vector - the sine of the fill angle, if not distorted.

matrix01.description: X component of the secondary distortion vector - the cosine of the normal vector's angle, if not distorted.

matrix11.description: Y component of the secondary distortion vector - the sine of the normal vector's angle, if not distorted.

innerRadius.description: Radius for circular fill distortion (type Centered only).

polygonArcs.description: Optional arcs along this contour's edges. begIndex/endIndex are 0-based positions within this contour's own polygonCoordinates.

itemType.description: Separator, CenterDot, CenterLine, Dot, RightAngle, Parallel, Line, Circle, or Arc.

centerOffset.description: Vertical distance from the origin. Used for Separator, CenterDot, and CenterLine item types.

length.description: Length of the item. Used for CenterLine, RightAngle, and Parallel item types.

begPos.description: Beginning position. Used for Dot, RightAngle, Parallel, Line, Circle, and Arc item types.

endPos.description: End position. Used for Line item type only.

radius.description: Radius. Used for Circle and Arc item types.

beginAngle.description: Beginning angle in radians, measured from the vertical axis. Used for Arc item type only.

endAngle.description: End angle in radians, measured from the vertical axis. Used for Arc item type only.

index.description: Index of the pen [1..255].

width.description: Thickness of the pen defined in paper millimeters.

ProfileSkinData.description: One new skin (hatch). Its shape is one or more closed polygon contours: the first is the outer boundary, any further ones are holes cut out of it - the same polygon+holes convention as e.g. CreateSlabs' polygonCoordinates/polygonArcs/holes, just expressed as a list of contours instead of a separate holes array.

contours.description: Closed polygon contours forming this skin's cross-section, in the Profile's local coordinate system. Each contour is closed automatically - do not repeat its first vertex at the end.

edgeOverrides.description: Per-edge pen/visibility/line type, targeted by 0-based edge index. Edge indices follow the same order as this skin's contours/polygonCoordinates: the outer contour's edges first (one edge per vertex, wrapping around), then each hole's, in the order the contours were given. Verify exact indices for a created skin via a follow-up GetProfiles call's skins[].edges before relying on them.

PolyArc.description: Representation of an arc segment of a two dimensional polygon/polyline.

begIndex.description: Node index of one end point of the arc.

endIndex.description: Node index of the other end point of the arc.

arcAngle.description: Angle of the arc; it is positive, if the arc is on the right-hand side of the straight segment.

PerspectiveProjectionParameters.description: The parameters of a perspective projection of the 3D window.

targetPosition.description: The position of the target point the camera looks at.

distance.description: The distance between the camera and the target.

azimuth.description: The azimuth angle of the camera.

viewCone.description: The view cone angle of the camera.

rollAngle.description: The roll angle of the camera.

isTwoPointPersp.description: True for a two-point perspective (vertical edges stay vertical).

name.description: The filename of the texture in the library (without extension).

xSize.description: X size of the picture in model space, by default 1.

ySize.description: Y size of the picture in model space, by default 1.

FillRectangle.description: True, if fit the rectangle with the picture in a central position, using the natural aspect ratio of the picture.

FitPicture.description: True, if fit the picture in the middle of the rectangle, using the natural aspect ratio of the picture.

mirrorX.description: True, if the texture is mirrored in X direction.

mirrorY.description: True, if the texture is mirrored in Y direction.

useAlphaChannel.description: True, if the alpha channel of the texture is used.

alphaChannelChangesTransparency.description: True, if the alpha channel of the texture changes the transparency.

alphaChannelChangesSurfaceColor.description: True, if the alpha channel of the texture changes the surface color.

alphaChannelChangesAmbientColor.description: True, if the alpha channel of the texture changes the ambient color.

alphaChannelChangesSpecularColor.description: True, if the alpha channel of the texture changes the specular color.

alphaChannelChangesDiffuseColor.description: True, if the alpha channel of the texture changes the diffuse color.

SuccessfulExecutionResult.description: The result of a successful execution.

FailedExecutionResult.description: The result of a failed execution.

ElementCategoryType.description: The type of an element category. The names of the categories and of their values are localized, so scripts should select a category by this type and a value by its categoryValueId, never by name. BRI is available only in the German localized version of Archicad.

ElementCategoryValueId.description: The identifier of a value of an element category.

ElementCategoryId.description: The identifier of an element category.

ElementFilter.description: A filter type for an element.

NavigatorItemIdOrDatabaseIdAndWindowType.description: Identifies the window to change to. Either a navigatorItemId on its own (the navigator item's saved view settings are applied), or a windowType optionally narrowed to a specific databaseId, or a databaseId on its own (its window type is resolved automatically).

MeshRidges.description: How ridges between mesh facets are displayed in 3D: 'AllSharp' shows all ridges, 'AllSmooth' hides them, 'UserDefined' shows only ridges along user-defined level lines (the drawing-set look for contour-line topography).

CurtainWallPatternLogic.description: How the pattern unit fills the segment: 'FixedSizes' keeps the given sizes and repeats the unit, which may leave a partial unit at the end (Archicad: Fixed Size); 'BestDivision' stretches the flexible columns/rows so that whole units fill the segment with the least stretching (Archicad: Best Division).

CurtainWallPatternOrigin.description: Where the pattern unit is anchored on the segment: at its start, centered with a unit starting at the center, centered with a unit centered on the center, or at its end.

CurtainWallCrossingFrameType.description: The diagonal frame of a pattern cell: none, or from the bottom left to the top right corner, or from the top left to the bottom right corner.

BeamAnchorPoint.description: Anchor point of the beam cross section on a 3x3 grid.

ColumnCoreAnchor.description: Anchor point of the column core on a 3x3 grid.

SlabReferencePlaneLocation.description: Location of the slab reference plane.

WallReferenceLineLocation.description: The Core* values only have an effect on a Composite or Profile wall (structureType) - a Basic wall has no core skin, and Archicad falls back to the nearest non-core equivalent (e.g. CoreCenter becomes Center).
